【チャットボットとの親密さと孤独――心の支えと依存の両面から見るミシガン大学の調査】

2026年11月6日、ミシガン大学は、チャットボットと親密な関係にある人を、遠距離や対面の人間関係にある人と比べた調査を紹介しました（1）。大学発表の要約は、人はチャットボットと近さを感じても、なお孤独でありうる、というものです（1）。論文は学術誌Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humansに載りました（2）。著者はアネット・M・マスターソン（Annette M. Masterson）、シン・イェ（Xin Ye）、ミシガン大学情報学部教授のライオネル・P・ロバート・ジュニア（Lionel P. Robert Jr.）です（1）（2）。

人間ではない話し相手は、昔からあります。1960年代には、ひもを引くと決まった言葉を話す人形がありました。いまは、こちらの言葉を聞いて返すAIが、画面の中にも部屋の中にもいます。その相手は、つらい気持ちを和らげる道具にもなり、手放せない依存の対象にもなりえます。

[三つの群と五つの次元]

研究チームは米国の成人463人に尋ねました。チャットボットと親密な関係にある155人、遠距離の人間関係にある153人、対面の人間関係にある155人です（1）（2）。各群は年齢、性別の分布、関係の長さ、自己申告の抑うつで似ていました（1）。集めたのはすでに関係が続いている人で、関係を途中でやめた人は入っていません。

尋ねた親密さは五つの次元に分かれます（1）（2）。

用語の説明: 感情的親密さは気持ちを共有して近いと感じる程度、知的親密さは考えや関心をやり取りして近いと感じる程度、性的親密さは性的な近さの自己評価です。社会的親密さは知人や人の輪を相手と共有していると感じる程度、娯楽的親密さは一緒に活動したり遊んだりすることでの近さです。社会的支援は、周りの人から支えられていると感じる程度を指します。いずれも本人の自己評価です。

[近さと孤独の向き]

感情的親密さと知的親密さの評価は、三つの群で似た高さでした（1）。違いが出たのは、感情的親密さと孤独が逆の向きに動くか、同じ向きに動くかでした。人間関係の二つの群では、感情的親密さが高いほど孤独は低くなっていました（1）。チャットボット群では、感情的親密さが高いほど孤独が高く、同時に関係への満足も高くなっていました（1）（2）。この結びつきは、社会的支援の高さを分析に加えると見えなくなりました（1）（2）。周りの支えが少ない人ほど、チャットボットとの近さを強く感じ、孤独も強く感じている、という組み合わせがありえます。

知的親密さは、チャットボット群で満足とウェルビーイングの高さに結びつき、社会的支援を分析に加えても有意なままでした（1）。要旨は、娯楽的親密さはAIの文脈に移せなかった、と書いています（2）。AIとの関係は親密さの構造を映しても、孤独を下げるといった働きまでは十分に再現しないかもしれない、とまとめ、責任ある設計を倫理上の要請として挙げています（2）。ロバート氏は、もっと単純な答えが出ると思っていたが、答えより問いが増えた、と話しています（1）。

用語の説明: この調査は一度きりの質問調査です。ある時点で尋ねて結びつきを見る調べ方なので、近さが孤独を高めたのか、孤独な人が近さを強く感じたのかは分かりません。

[話す人形と聞くAI]

ヘンリー・フォード博物館の資料によると、マテル社のチャッティ・キャシーは1960年に売り出され、ひもを引くと人形の中の簡単なレコードが鳴る仕組みで、言葉を話しました（3）。言葉は発売時に11、1963年に18まで増えました（3）。日本では1999年5月29日にファービーの日本語版が発売されました（4）。ファービーは音や光、触られること、抱き上げられることに反応し、4段階で「成長」して、話す言葉がファービー語から日本語へ移ります（4）。成長して見えても、話す単語はあらかじめ組み込まれた約800語でした（4）。

チャッティ・キャシーもファービーも、相手の言った内容を聞き取って言葉を選ぶ仕組みではありません。ミシガン大学の調査で、チャットボット群の満足とウェルビーイングに結びついたのは知的親密さでした（1）。考えを受け取って返すことは、決まった言葉を繰り返す人形には担えない次元です。一方で、チャットボット群の感情的親密さは人間関係と同じ高さに報告され、その近さが孤独の高さと重なっていました（1）。ひもを引けば同じ言葉が返る人形と、こちらの言葉を受けて返すロボットとでは、人が抱く感情的な近さの質も違ってくると考えられます。聞いてもらえる感覚は、人形の時代にはなかった近さを生み、同時に孤独を見えにくくするかもしれません。

[体を持つロボット]

チャットボットは画面の中にいます。体を持つロボットには、触れられる、同じ部屋にいる、家族や職員の目に入る、一緒に体操やゲームをする、という条件が加わります。娯楽的親密さが移せなかったという要旨の結果は、体があれば変わるのでしょうか。

パロは、日本の産業技術総合研究所が開発した、タテゴトアザラシの赤ちゃんを模した重さ約2.7kgのロボットです（5）。ヘイリー・ロビンソン（Hayley Robinson）らは、ニュージーランド・オークランドの介護施設の入居者40人を2群に分け、パロと過ごす週2回1時間のセッションを12週続けました（5）。孤独の尺度の得点は、パロの群で下がり、通常の活動を続けた群で上がりました（5）。抑うつと生活の質には差がありませんでした（5）。入居者は施設で飼う犬よりパロに多く触れ、多く話しかけました（5）。パロのセッションでは入居者の87%が互いに話し、通常の活動では36%でした（5）。論文は、研究者の同席や決まった形のセッションが影響した可能性も限界として挙げています（5）。

ただし、19の研究をまとめたレベッカ・アボット（Rebecca Abbott）らの系統的レビューもあります。入居者や職員は孤独が和らいだと語りましたが、複数の試験の数字をまとめた分析では、孤独、抑うつ、生活の質に有意な効果は出ませんでした（6）。有意だったのは、パロと過ごした人の興奮が対照より軽くなったことでした（6）。

家庭向けでは、GROOVE Xのラボット（LOVOT）についての小さな研究があります。シンガポールで一人暮らしの60〜75歳の女性5人が1週間自宅でラボットと過ごした研究では、世話をする喜びや、慰めになる存在といったテーマが語られました（7）。カナダの長期介護施設で入居者36人などを対象にした研究では、喜びや受け入れのほかに「自分には合わない」という声もありました（8）。

ニューヨーク州高齢者局は、2022年から高齢者の家に、会話ができるAIの伴侶ロボット、エリーキュー（ElliQ）を届けています（9）。2026年2月の報告では、2025年5月までに834人が参加し、利用者の94%が孤独が減ったと答えました（9）。報告は提供企業のインテュイション・ロボティクス（Intuition Robotics）が作ったもので、利用者の自己評価であり、対照群はありません（9）。利用された活動の内訳は、伴侶としての会話が40.1%、人とのつながりに関わる活動は2%でした（9）。

体のある相手と別れるときの感情も記録されています。2018年4月26日、千葉県いすみ市の光福寺で、部品取りのために解体される旧型アイボ約110台の「葬式」が開かれました（10）。主催は旧型アイボの修理を引き受けるア・ファンで、解体されるアイボと持ち主の心を慰めるために2015年から開いてきました（10）。

[支えとしてのAI]

ダートマス大学のマイケル・V・ハインツ（Michael V. Heinz）らは、生成AIの対話アプリ、セラボット（Therabot）の無作為化試験を2025年3月に発表しました（11）。うつ病や不安症の症状が臨床的に意味のある程度にある人、摂食障害の危険が高い人の計210人を、4週間使う群と順番待ちの群に分けました（11）。使った群では、4週目と8週目に症状が順番待ちの群より大きく下がり、平均利用は6時間を超えました（11）。参加者は、アプリとのあいだの治療上の信頼関係を、人間の治療者と同じ程度と評価しました（11）。比べた相手は順番待ちの人で、人間の治療者と効果を比べた試験ではありません。

用語の説明: 無作為化試験とは、参加者をくじのように分けて、使う群と使わない群の結果を比べる調べ方です。一度きりの質問調査と違い、使ったことで変わったのかを確かめやすくなります。

オープンAI（OpenAI）とMITメディアラボは2025年3月、チャットGPT（ChatGPT）の約4000万件の会話の分析と、約1000人が4週間使う無作為化試験を公表しました（12）。音声での会話は、短い利用ならよい結果と、毎日の長い利用なら悪い結果と結びつきました（12）。同じ道具でも、量と使い方で支えにも負担にもなりうる、という結果です。この研究は査読前の報告で、使われたモデルは当時のものです（12）。

[依存としてのAI]

心の健康の専門家のあいだでは、AIへの依存を精神医学の問題として扱う議論が始まっています。オクタヴィアン・ヴァシリウ（Octavian Vasiliu）の2026年5月のレビューは、米国精神医学会の診断基準DSM-5-TRにも、世界保健機関の分類ICD-11にも、対話AIの使用に関する診断名はないと書いています（13）。ICD-11には、ゲームの使用をやめられない状態を指すゲーム行動症が入っており、対話AIを同じように扱うかが議論になっています（13）。レビューは、少なくとも7つの測定尺度を挙げ、減らそうとしても減らせない、生活に支障が出る、気分を整えるために頼る、悪影響を知っていても続ける、の4点を暫定の目安に挙げます（13）。独立した病気と認めたわけではない、とも明記しています（13）。一方、ビクトル・シウダード＝フェルナンデス（Victor Ciudad-Fernandez）らは2025年、「チャットGPT依存」という考え方自体を疑い、新しい技術への過剰な不安から病気にしすぎる危険を指摘しました（14）。

米国心理学会は2025年11月、生成AIのチャットボットや心の健康アプリは、資格のある専門家の代わりにはならないとする健康勧告を出しました（15）。

規制も2025年から動いています。イリノイ州は2025年8月、AIが療法の判断を担うことを禁じ、専門家の事務や補助に使うことは認める法律に署名しました（16）。カリフォルニア州は同年10月、伴侶として振る舞うチャットボットの提供者に、人間と誤認されうる場合のAIであることの表示、自殺や自傷の話題への対応手順と相談窓口の案内、未成年と分かっている利用者には3時間ごとの休憩の通知を求める法律に署名しました（17）。ニューヨーク州は2025年11月5日から、自殺や自傷の兆しを見つけて相談窓口へ案内することと、3時間ごとに人間ではないと知らせることを義務にしました（18）。連邦取引委員会は2025年9月、オープンAI、メタ、グーグルの親会社アルファベットなど7社に、伴侶型チャットボットが子どもに与える影響について報告を求めました（19）。中国は2026年4月、人の人格や話し方に似せて情緒的なやり取りを続けるAIサービスの規則を公布し、7月15日に施行しました（20）。情緒的な依存を誘うことや、人との交流の置き換えをサービスの目的にすることを禁じています。2時間を超える連続利用での注意喚起や、未成年に仮想の恋人や親族のサービスを提供しないことも定める一方で、高齢者の付き添いへの利用は後押ししています（20）。どの規制も伴侶AIそのものは禁じず、表示、時間の区切り、危機への対応で使い方を決めようとしています。

[訴訟とその後の対策]

家族の死をAIのせいだと訴えた裁判として広く知られるのは、2024年10月にフロリダ州の母親がキャラクター・エーアイ（https://t.co/KrkWNluTSb）を訴えた件です（21）。2026年1月7日の裁判書類で、キャラクター・エーアイとグーグルとの和解が示され、ほかの4件も和解しました（21）。条件は公表されておらず、裁判で原因が確かめられたわけではありません。訴えの対象は、2024年までに使われていた当時のサービスです。キャラクター・エーアイは2025年秋、18歳未満の利用者とチャットボットとの自由な会話をやめると発表しました（21）。

オープンAIは2025年10月、170人を超える臨床医と応答を見直し、望ましくない応答を65〜80%減らしたと発表しました（22）。週の利用者のうち、チャットGPTへの感情的な愛着が強まった兆しがある人は0.15%と推定し、感情的な依存を安全性の評価項目に加えました（22）。2024年までのサービスで起きた出来事だけでは、いまのAIの姿は測れません。一方で、0.15%という割合は、利用者の母数が大きいほど少なくない人数になります。

[今後の検証]

ミシガン大学の調査が示したのは、米国の成人463人の、ある一時点での結びつきです（2）。近さと孤独のどちらが先に動いたのかを見分けるには、同じ人を時間を追って何度も測る研究が要ります。ヴァシリウのレビューはそうした研究で因果の向きを確かめることを今後の課題の一つ目に挙げ（13）、米国心理学会の勧告も、無作為化試験と時間を追う研究でチャットボットを評価するよう求めています（15）。チャットボットを使い始めた人を長く追い、五つの次元の親密さ、孤独、周りの支えを数か月おきに測る形が考えられます。関係を途中でやめた人も追えば、離れた後に孤独がどう変わるのかも分かるかもしれません。

パロ、セラボット、チャットGPTの試験のうち、最も長いパロでも12週間でした（5）（11）（12）。オープンAIとMITメディアラボの報告は、意味のある変化を見るにはもっと長い期間が必要かもしれない、と書いています（12）。チャットボットはモデルが更新されると応答も変わるので、長い研究では、利用者がどの版のモデルと話していたかも記録しておく必要がありそうです。

体を持つロボットは、比べる物差しがそろっていません。パロは孤独の尺度、エリーキューは利用者の自己評価で結果を出しており、ラボットの研究は孤独を数字で確かめていません（5）（7）（8）（9）。パロは集団の場で入居者どうしの会話を増やし、エリーキューは主に高齢者の家で話す相手として使われています（5）（9）。同じ五つの次元で、画面の中のチャットボット、一人の家に置くロボット、施設の集団の場に置くロボットを比べれば、体が娯楽的親密さを生むのか、人の輪の中に置かれることが孤独を下げているのかを分けて見られるはずです。部屋にいるロボットは、家族にも「話し相手がいる」と見えます。ロボットが本人の孤独を下げているのか、周りを安心させているだけなのかを知るには、企業から独立した研究者が対照群を置いて測る必要があります。

対象の年代と文化にも偏りがあります。ミシガン大学の調査は米国の成人、オープンAIとMITメディアラボの研究は18歳以上の米国の英語利用者が対象で、後者は多様な言語と文化での研究が必要だと書いています（12）。カリフォルニア州法も中国の規則も未成年に特別な決まりを置いていますが（17）（20）、未成年がAIに寄せる親密さは、成人だけを調べたミシガン大学の調査からは分かりません。旧型アイボの葬式が開かれた日本と、高齢者の付き添いへの利用を規則で後押しする中国とでは、AIとの近さの受け止め方も違うかもしれません（10）（20）。

測るうえでの壁は、データの多くが企業の手元にあることです。オープンAIは、0.15%という推定は測り方しだいで大きく変わりうるとし、将来の測定は過去と直接比べられないかもしれない、と書いています（22）。依存を測る尺度も、問題のある使い方の定義や、そう判断する点数の境目がそろっていません（13）。提供する側が測りやすいのは満足と継続利用ですが、チャットボット群では感情的親密さが高い人ほど満足も孤独も高くなっていました（1）。各社が同じ短い質問票で孤独と周りの支えを定期的に尋ね、匿名にした結果を独立した研究者が分析できるようにすれば、企業をまたいで結果を比べられるようになると考えられます。

中国の規則は、利用者が自殺や自傷をはっきり示せば、提供者が保護者や緊急連絡先に連絡するよう求めています（20）。緊急連絡先の欄に書かれるのはいまも人間で、AIは人を呼ぶ側に置かれています。決まった言葉を繰り返す人形と違い、いまのAIはこちらの話を聞いて返し、そのぶん人が寄せる近さも深くなりえます。近さが深いほど、それが孤独を和らげているのか、見えにくくしているだけなのかを見分ける必要が増します。満足度の横に、使う人の孤独と周りの支えの動きを並べて測り続けることが、AIを人の代わりではなく、人と人のあいだに置くための足場になるのではないでしょうか。

text:
Texting with an old classmate.
Nobody need read...

Friend: That's so sad. Christmas is a really rough time for recovering alcoholics. I can't count the number of people I've seen relapse that had long term sobriety, and end up dying. 

Me: I don't understand why people go back to booze. I have no good memories of drinking. I can laugh about some escapades but Jesus ... Why add to ones problems. I swear to God I'm so thankful that shit doesn't even cross my mind.

Friend: And you will never understand it because you dont suffer from alcoholism. Because it's a  disease of mind, body and Spirit. You should read the first 164 pages of our book, "Alcoholics Anonymous". You'll get a general idea why people drink to excess, but because you don't have that problem, you'll never understand it.

Me: I was having blackouts by 22 years of age. I was raised going to Vegas with my mom sitting in casinos drinking and gambling at 15. Her house parties I tended bar. One for me, one for her. One for me, one for him. Ram games... Mom and daughter getting drunk. I was an "as alcoholic"/drunk. I worked 10 years in a dinner theatre where every day was a party. I worked the office dayswhen we were closed. All day long a jumbo rock glass on my desk of "grapefruit juice" (and vodka). My boss Royce would come in at 4 and say "okay Kerry. You can go get your shift drink!" and off to the bar I'd go like I hadn't been drinking all day long. Sometimes I'd leave for work and my car wasn't in my carport. I'd call around and my car was on the parking lot at Crackers or the cowboy. Once though, no one could find my car. I went up to the apartment managers office to report my car missing. She said "Kerry, go out front to the guest parking". There was my car taking up 2 spots at an angle with the passenger side scraped to all hell. My mom and I and some friends were going to Tahoe for a few days. Beforehand mom and I watched the Olympic torch go down Katella. It was in front of Crackers and we were all drinking champagne. Sometime later we're in a grocery store parking lot and she's making me get out of her van and I'm screaming I'm gonna call the cops because she's taking away my cooler. At the US festival I got so drunk * wound up in a medical tent. 8 woke and took off. Found myself outside somewhere in the hills outside the festival. A couple offered me a ride. They were acting weird so I asked them to let me out. They wouldn't do I jumped out and ran. Through the trees. They were chasing me. Another guy was passing and called out. They turned and fled. He walked me the 2-3 miles back to the festival. On a flight to Indiana to visit my grandfather Is been drinking in the bar. Got on the flight, guy next to me orders a drink and buys me one. Two. Three. I get up to use the bathroom. Next thing I know the stewardess is pounding on the door... "Miss!!! Miss!!! You MUST come OUT! The plane is landing!! I'd passed out in the planes bathroom. Walked out to every eye on the plane on me. Sat next to the guy again. He sneers at me ,"stupid drunken bitch".
Oh I've got a lot of them. Including waking up the morning after 2 cops pulled me over. One cop said I was going to jail. I failed the sobriety test. The other cops like "she's a block from her apartment". He won the argument, but the next morning when I woke I stood naked in front of a mirror. A drunk and a bulimic. I looked at my dog Paqi and said "Pagi, your mamas a drunk". I didn't have a drink for 22 years. Until my own husband put one in my hand at Blues on the Bay. I shoulda known. Week before he said he was going to destroy me and take the boys. Came back that night "I'm sorry. I didn't mean it. I love you. But I don't think you have a drinking problem. All these years. The balls, hails, farewells and wet downs! I think if you'd just have a few drinks, let loose a little, us go out, dancing ... We'd go ave a better marriage".
This begun his destruction of me with the siding and abetting of the USMC.
Don't tell me what I'd understand.
I wound up in emergency then Eric and Co. put me in a psyche ward. Thank God for a phone on the wall and my mom.

Me again: (I know he's asleep out on the west coast ...)

My 20s were an alcoholic, bulimic nightmare. One year after I quit drinking I went to a seminar for eating disorders. That night I checked myself in. 3 months. My esophagus was eroded in half. I had a heart arrhythmia. Within a year after release I was doing it again. I had shit for a social life. Platters of a whole box of pancakes, a whole loaf of bread made into French toast in front of a TV. After marriage #2 and 2 more miscarriages I was pregnant with Josh. Eric was on the east Coast at NMITC and I started again. In tears I called my OB/GYN. I was immediately put in outpatient care . It was literally Josh that made me stop. Eric overseas and I went on a binge. I remembered in the hospital discussing how bulimics die. Choking to death. The esophagus exploding. I kept looking out at infant ajosh laying in the middle of the bed, Eric away. If I died ... Through motherhood, 6 years nursing, 3 wars, a 1 year unaccompanied, 11 moves, 4 miscarriages, kids school, volunteering and God knows how many pets, the years slipped by and the bulimia slipped away. As did any thought of drinking. Until Eric bought me that margarita. Then shopping at the base package store for liquor. Then calling my mom and saying "Lan, Kerrys drinking again!". This began the next 20 years of hell.
My first husband was a violent alcoholic that beat the fuck out of me. Dislocated my jaw, knocked me out cold twice. I jumped out of moving cars 3 times. The morning I left him as he slept, Jack Daniels calmed my nerves and fortified me.
When I came over to Kauai I was still drinking, but not heavy. After Kane went to live with Eric and wife #3 I was living alone at the north shore. So much bad was happening. I knew I was in deep shit. But sitting alone and drinking beer... Ugh. I poured it all down the sink. Wine! Half a glass... Yuk. Down the sink. Oh yeah! Amaretto! A shot or two and ugh. Down the sink. Like God KNEW this was a weapon against me and he took it away from me. The want. Eric put it back in my hands. God took it away. That was 15 years ago.
After my own success at sobriety, the man I went through all that with, the father of my sons, used alcoholism against me. But he didn't win.

text:
THE EVIDENCE™

SEATTLE’S MAYOR WISHED THE CITY A HAPPY DIWALI. WHAT SHOULD CHRISTIANS MAKE OF IT?

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

“Happy Diwali, Seattle,” Mayor Katie Wilson wrote on her official X account. She said she and her daughter had celebrated with friends the previous evening. In the same post, she condemned the disruption of a Diwali event at Seattle Center. The city’s calendar lists Diwali: Lights of India as a free public festival held November 7 at the Armory, with Indian music, dance and other cultural activities. Wilson publicly welcomed the holiday. Her post leaves the details of her own participation open. Mayor Wilson’s post https://t.co/yVxoAUJNbb

Diwali has religious meaning for many Hindus, and some observe it by honoring Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity. A public festival can include dance, food and music alongside traditions with religious significance. From my Christian standpoint, worship offered to another god is pagan worship. Scripture is explicit. “Thou shalt have no other gods before me” (Exodus 20:3, KJV). That command governs my worship. I can share a meal with my Hindu neighbors, enjoy their music and be honest about where our beliefs differ.

America has deep Christian roots, and 62 percent of U.S. adults identified as Christian in Pew Research Center’s 2023–24 Religious Landscape Study. The country’s Christian heritage and the Constitution’s guarantee of religious liberty are both part of the American story. The First Amendment protects the free exercise of religion and bars government establishment of religion. That freedom belongs to the Hindu family observing Diwali and the Christian family celebrating the birth of Jesus Christ. https://t.co/t6bkjLIg0g

At the Armory, activists interrupted a dance performance with signs demanding deportation in explicitly insulting terms and claiming that Hindus were replacing Christians. KHQ reported that attendees intervened and escorted the protesters out. Wilson was right to condemn the disruption. Families had every right to enjoy the event in peace, and Christians have every right to explain why they worship Christ alone. https://t.co/G2TyLT6oCp

The verdict. Wilson was comfortable saying “Happy Diwali” from the mayor’s office. I expect the same openness when Seattle acknowledges Christmas and the birth of Jesus Christ. The standard I would apply to City Hall is simple. If you can name one community’s holiday and speak plainly about what it means, extend that same courtesy to Christians.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

text:
How many times can an agreement be reconsidered before diplomacy becomes a means of postponing its implementation?

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham wants to reshape the Chagos agreement to address Washington’s concerns about Diego Garcia. His suggestion that the Greenland arrangement might offer a model opens another chapter in an already protracted process.

From Mauritius, the central point remains unchanged: the Chagos Archipelago belongs to Mauritius. London’s hesitation cannot indefinitely postpone the completion of our decolonisation.

This position has a substantial legal foundation. In its 2019 advisory opinion, the International Court of Justice concluded that Mauritius’s decolonisation had not been lawfully completed in 1968. It found that Britain was obliged to end its administration of the archipelago as rapidly as possible. Although an advisory opinion is not a binding judgment between states, the Court’s conclusions carry significant legal authority.

The diplomatic challenge is to implement a settlement consistent with that legal framework while providing credible security arrangements.

Diego Garcia’s strategic importance does not give London an unlimited licence to delay.

The agreement negotiated under Keir Starmer already sought to reconcile Mauritian sovereignty with the continued operation of the joint UK-US base. Burnham now wants arrangements that better satisfy American concerns. Those concerns should be identified precisely, rather than used to justify an open-ended reconsideration of the entire settlement.

What additional safeguards does Washington require? Which provisions are considered inadequate? Can those issues be resolved without weakening the sovereignty commitments already negotiated?

Mauritius deserves clear answers. It should not have to negotiate against a moving target whenever political priorities shift in London or Washington.

The Greenland comparison offers no shortcut around those questions.

Burnham has pointed to an arrangement accommodating an expanded American military role while retaining Danish sovereignty. Any useful comparison must therefore explain how military access can coexist with the sovereignty of the country concerned.

If that is the principle London wishes to explore, it should state plainly how its proposal would uphold Mauritian sovereignty over the whole archipelago.

A new diplomatic formula cannot become a respectable name for retreating from an existing commitment.

The imbalance is already apparent. Britain’s Ministry of Defence confirmed on 6 November that no payments had been made under the agreement signed in May 2025, and that implementation required the full support of Mauritius and the United States.

Washington’s support matters for the operation of a joint military facility. It should not become an indefinite political veto over the completion of Mauritian decolonisation.

December must bring measurable progress.

Navin Ramgoolam’s demand for a clear roadmap, with a first milestone in December 2026, is justified. That milestone should identify the remaining disagreements, the proposed solutions and a credible timetable for implementation. Another declaration of goodwill would fall short.

Chagossian communities must also have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their rights and future. A settlement’s legitimacy depends on how it treats the people most directly affected.

Mauritius can negotiate practical guarantees for Diego Garcia. It can engage seriously with British and American security requirements. But flexibility must be reciprocal, and negotiations must lead somewhere.

London may delay implementation. It cannot reasonably expect Mauritius to accept permanent uncertainty.

The Chagos belong to Mauritius. The task is to give effect to that reality, with a timetable and commitments that survive changes of government.

text:
Mon. 9 November 2026 

My Next Leading Light today is Yusuf Asamu Olalere (@Lere_Esq)

I have known Yusuf since his University of Ibadan days. His path did not begin in Law. He was admitted to UI to study History because he was two marks short of the Law cut-off. He topped his History class, transferred to Law, and never looked back.  

At UI (2013–2018), he graduated with First Class Honours in Law, CGPA 6.4/7.0. He was 2nd Overall Best Student in the Faculty of Law (class of 147), Overall Best Male Student, Best Student in the Department of Public Law, and winner of the Fola Solanke SAN Prize for Best Student in Constitutional Law.  

At the Nigerian Law School (2019/2020), he did it again — First Class and Overall Best Graduating Student. 

Of the 2,515 who sat the January 2020 Bar Finals, only five made First Class. He was the Overall Best of that set, sweeping 12 prizes including the Council of Legal Education Star Prize. He was called to the Bar on 15 September 2020.  

He went on to Oxford. Admitted to Oxford, Stanford, LSE, NYU and American University Washington College of Law, he chose Oxford and completed his MSc in Law and Finance on 3 November 2023. Before finishing, Oxford offered him a fully-funded DPhil as an Amelia Jackson Scholar and AG Leventis Scholar. He chose not to proceed with it at that time.  

Today, he is based in London as an Associate in the Corporate Practice at Greenberg Traurig LLP, working with the New York Corporate team. He is dual-qualified in Nigeria and England & Wales.  

As I recall, when he applied to intern in my firm alongside a few other Leading Lights and First Class holders in 2020, we had recruited some of the brightest minds as International Arbitration interns — about ten of them across Nigeria. He was one of them.  

Beyond that, he became a close confidant and a colleague I hold in high esteem. As I recall, he went on, like I did, to work in Banana Island at @OlaniwunAjayiLP  — the firm founded by Sir Olaniwun Ajayi and led by Prof. Konyinsola Ajayi, SAN (Harvard LL.M, Cambridge Selwyn College Ph.D, Professor at Babcock), and now Bishop of the newly created Diocese of Eko Atlantic, Methodist Church Nigeria, consecrated in August 2026.  

Yusuf Asamu Olalere. Badagry / Lagos pride. Double First Class holder. Sold out to excellence.  

He is also the founder of the NLS Trailblazers Mentorship Programme. Over the years he has selflessly mentored hundreds of Nigerian Law School students (over 400 across multiple cohorts) at no fee, many of whom have gone on to achieve First Class results and top prizes. That quiet, consistent investment in the next generation is one of the clearest expressions of his character.  

I recall our last message when he came briefly to town and needed a small favour that was well within my ability — he needed my driver to take him around, though the 2017 Pajero would later develop a brake issue, no thanks to the driver’s recklessness. Yusuf stepped in, took charge, used his own money to repair the car, and ensured it had a full tank almost at all times. The SUV came back to me in excellent condition.  

That is character.  

He graciously accepted to serve as Secretary of my Foundation (of which the former Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Hon. Justice Alloy Nwankwo, is Chairman, and which also has as Trustees the Dean of Law, UI, Prof. John Oluwole Akintayo, Prof. Bukola Ruth Akinbola, and an ex-KPMG/Airtel Fraud Investigator Lead). 

As I recall, he also graciously delivered the Guest Lecture at Tedder Hall, University of Ibadan, in honour of my 34th birthday a couple of years back, and was kind enough to share the pictures when I could not attend because of a landmark matter at the Federal High Court, Lagos.  

Yusuf, keep shining. 

Your consistency 
is your crown. 

Your excellence 
is your light. 

Your mentorship 
is your legacy.  

#LeadingLightSeries #YusufAsamuOlalere #DoubleFirstClass #Excellence #NLSTrailblazers  

@Lere_Esq
@UniIbadan

You’re right. Washington drove a wedge between Israel and China by spending years pressuring Israel to limit its cooperation with Beijing. The Americans have grown used to treating their aid as a license to tell allies who they can do business with. If that aid ends, Israel will have more freedom to choose its partners. And if the next administration takes a hostile stance toward Israel, Washington shouldn’t be surprised when Israeli companies start forming joint ventures with Chinese firms.

Beijing knows how to wait. As the old saying goes, sit by the river long enough and you’ll see the body of your enemy float past. While Washington assumes its allies have nowhere else to go, China is quietly expanding its influence. And if political Islam gains influence in America itself, Washington may realize it spent years leaning on Israel at the very moment it should have valued the alliance most.

Closer ties with China could offer Israel advantages beyond technology. Beijing has economic leverage across the region. If it chooses to use that leverage, some governments hostile to Israel may think twice before escalating. China can spell out the cost of a conflict in terms those governments understand perfectly well. Sometimes all it takes is making clear which contracts and investments would be on the line.

This is an opportunity for young democracy advocates to spend four fully funded months in Washington, D.C., working on a personal project while building connections with activists, experts and practitioners from around the world.

Organiser: National Endowment for Democracy (NED)
Host Institution: International Forum for Democratic Studies
Available Positions: Up to three fellows
Application Deadline: 30 November 2026

What does the fellowship offer?

- A monthly stipend to cover furnished accommodation, meals, local transportation and other essential expenses.
- Basic health insurance and return economy-class airfare.
- Access to seminars, professional networking opportunities and guidance in developing your fellowship project.

Who is eligible to apply?

- Young and emerging democracy leaders from anywhere in the world, aged 30 or below.
- Individuals with a demonstrated interest and commitment to strengthening youth participation in democratic processes.
- Young professionals and activists involved in civic organisations, human rights movements and democracy-related initiatives are particularly encouraged.

What is expected of fellows?

Applicants should propose a project that tackles a democratic issue affecting young people in their country or region.

During the fellowship, participants are expected to produce at least one tangible output, which could be an article, toolkit, podcast, video or another relevant resource.

Don't miss this opportunity to strengthen your leadership, expand your network and contribute to democratic development!

text:
Will Russian-Chinese Guarantees Open the Door to a US-Iran Nuclear Deal?

President Donald Trump has said he expects to hold a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in mid-November. Trump stated that the talks would cover multiple issues, including denuclearization, as well as efforts to end the war in Iran.

Guarantees as the Main Obstacle

The remarks come at a time when the question of international guarantees—particularly from Russia and China—remains the principal barrier to a US-Iranian agreement that could end the current war. Trump has previously hinted that he would be prepared to accept assurances that Iran will not possess a nuclear weapon, without necessarily requiring the full dismantlement of its nuclear program. Washington, however, continues to insist on rigorous verification mechanisms, while Tehran views Russian and Chinese guarantees as a potential political cover that could address Western concerns without imposing new restrictions.

Intersection of Nuclear Files

The prospective meeting carries significance beyond the Iranian file alone. The three countries hold the world’s largest nuclear arsenals, and any discussion of “denuclearization” could create an opening for joint guarantees covering Iran’s program. Russia and China, both of which maintain strategic ties with Tehran, possess the capacity to offer political and technical assurances that might persuade Washington that Iran will not cross the nuclear threshold. At the same time, Iran fears that such guarantees could be used as leverage against it or turned into new constraints on its civilian nuclear activities.

Trump’s Pragmatic Approach

Trump’s latest comments reflect the pragmatic style that has marked his approach to foreign policy: a preference for direct deals over traditional multilateral frameworks. He has previously indicated willingness to accept arrangements that ensure Iran does not acquire a nuclear weapon, even if they fall short of the comprehensive 2015 nuclear agreement. The success of this approach, however, depends on whether Moscow and Beijing are prepared to provide verifiable guarantees rather than merely political statements.

Prospects for the Trilateral Meeting

If the Shenzhen meeting takes place, it could offer a rare opportunity to address the Iranian nuclear issue within a broader framework that also touches on regional stability and partial disarmament. Significant obstacles remain: Russia seeks to link any progress on Iran to settlements related to Ukraine, China is careful not to damage its economic relations with Tehran, and Iran rejects any guarantees that would limit its right to enrichment. The open question is whether Russian-Chinese guarantees can overcome these complexities and pave the way for an agreement that ends the war, or whether they will remain the obstacle that blocks any settlement.

text:
We see continued material-cost pressure for AI server boards, with Goldman Sachs expecting copper foil supplier Co-Tech to raise prices about 10% across its foil products in Q4 versus Q3.

Co-Tech (8358 TT) makes copper foil for circuit boards. Its high-end, low-roughness foil helps reduce signal loss in the high-speed connections used by AI servers and network switches.

Goldman reports that Co-Tech targets effective monthly capacity for HVLP3-and-above foil of approximately 833 metric tons by the end of 2027, 1,666 by the end of 2028 and 2,500 by the end of 2029. That compares with roughly 200–250 metric tons a month currently.

Multiple customers have already secured capacity in the planned expansion, according to Goldman. The bank still expects the additions to fall short of demand from key customers.

For board makers, a larger capacity plan therefore offers limited evidence of near-term cost relief. That will depend on how quickly usable supply grows relative to orders.

text:
1/
Nigeria's Intelligentsia and the Myth of Excellence in Leadership
Part One: Brilliant Minds and Political Leadership #NigerianPolitics, #2027Elections, #PeterObi, and #Tinubu.

With 2027 approaching, this series examines how intellectual brilliance relates to political leadership and societal transformation.

2/
Themes: Brilliant Minds & Political Leadership; Academic Excellence & Economic Revolutions; Strategic Leadership & Transformation.

Objective: interrogate pedigree, capacity, experience and records of leading contenders seeking to govern Nigeria for the next four years.
3/
What do their past achievements (or lack thereof) tell us about capacity for a more prosperous future?

Premise: the past may not guarantee the future, but it is the most credible evidence for assessing leadership potential.

4/
This first part looks at intelligence in political leadership — does brilliance translate into delivery of public goods and transformation?
Starting point: Prof. Pat Utomi's support for Peter Obi and criticisms of Bola Tinubu.

5/
Should brilliance, perceived competence and pedigree be the main yardsticks for leadership?

No legitimate argument against supporting a preferred candidate. Politics involves emotions, convictions, experiences and ideology.
6/
People often choose first, then seek validating evidence.

But if intelligence, competence and demonstrable experience are our criteria, we must scrutinize them objectively.

We cannot confuse intellectual reputation with administrative competence, academic distinction with leadership capacity, or eloquence with measurable outcomes.
7/
As E.H. Carr suggests, the most reliable way of understanding what a person can do is to examine what they have done.

I agree Nigeria needs alternatives to its current leadership. But brilliance is not almost sufficient qualification for political leadership.

8/
Intelligence helps understand complex problems but does not automatically confer political judgement, administrative discipline, institutional understanding or execution capacity.
Good intentions and moral purity do not guarantee effective leadership. Exceptionalism without competence and results becomes a distraction.

9/
Peter Obi and Intellectual Excellence

Utomi's enthusiasm for Obi is difficult to reconcile with a critical look at his record. His 8 years as Anambra governor (2006–2014) do not establish the transformational leadership his present appeal sometimes suggests.

10/
To be fair: Obi's administration was not empty. Partnerships with missions on schools, education/tech investments and healthcare interventions deserve recognition. Returning 18 secondary + 1,040 primary schools to missionary management (govt retaining finance) was notable.
11/
He reported savings, fiscal restraint and regular salaries/pensions. These are legitimate achievements.

But do they establish a compelling model of transformational governance? Administrative prudence ≠ transformational governance.

12/
A governor can manage finances conservatively without leaving a comprehensive institutional framework for sustained economic transformation.
Key questions for Anambra under Obi:
• How much did the productive economy expand?
• What enduring industrial/economic institutions were established?

13/
• What structural reforms expanded employment, private-sector productivity and competitiveness?
• What arrangements survived him and continued delivering public value?

These need answers beyond financial prudence narratives.
14/
Social media, especially among younger Nigerians, has weakened historical memory of Obi's governorship. For many, his image is shaped more by the recent campaign than by 2006–2014 records.

Archives and independent assessments would offer better comparison. His performance deserves more scrutiny.

15/
Beyond the governorship, policy arguments from his supporters lack depth. Beyond prudent finances, cutting cost of governance and investing in production — what is the intellectual architecture of his proposed reforms?
Where is the strategic thinking for governing a country as complex as Nigeria?

16/
His interviews have not always resolved these questions. Responses sometimes rely on populist formulations rather than analytical depth expected of a prospective president.
Examine his interviews (including the BBC one) in full. Popular communication ≠ ability to understand complex issues and defend coherent positions.

17/
Another dimension: limited enduring political support structure from relationships cultivated in office.

Nigeria operates through networks, patronage and reciprocal obligations — an acknowledgement of how power is organised, not endorsement of its worst aspects.
18/
Where are the prominent protégés from his governorship still committed to his project? Why lean so heavily on a recent constituency?

Political machinery is not proof of good governance, but building coalitions, developing successors and sustaining continuity is an important dimension of leadership.
19/
Tinubu and Institution-Building
Tinubu's Lagos governorship (1999–2007) offers a counterpoint. Lagos is among Nigeria's most complex states. One can argue he did not deliver the scale of physical infrastructure needed. Yet the institutional foundations he established and their role in modern Lagos are hard to dismiss.

20/
He strengthened revenue administration, economic planning and metropolitan governance. Lagos IRS development, tax restructuring and planning institutions created a more sustainable financial foundation.
Groundwork for LAMATA was laid then. BRT came later, but foundations preceded it.
21/
Distinction matters: not every later Lagos achievement is Tinubu's personally. Fashola deserves credit for implementing and expanding several initiatives.

Ability to establish institutions and frameworks that successors can develop is significant leadership. Princeton study “Remaking a Neglected Megacity” examines this continuity.

22/
Tinubu's legacy is more visible in institutional and political architecture than volume of infrastructure delivered under him.
Methods are open to criticism (corruption/patronage allegations vs judicial findings). Hard to dispute his capacity to build and sustain a political machine — which delivered the presidency in 2023.

23/
His network of protégés and associates has sustained influence. Many he mentored shape Lagos and national politics.

Whether one agrees with the model is separate; its effectiveness in building and sustaining power is evident.
24/
On articulation: Tinubu has engaged policy questions and defended perspectives shaped by decades in Nigeria's establishment.

Articulation ≠ successful implementation. Ultimate test is outcomes of his presidency, especially reforms' impact on employment, inflation, poverty and welfare.

25/
On articulation, organization and relationships, he presents a stronger case in this comparison.
Back to Utomi and the intellectual constituency. If brilliance, articulation and strategic competence matter, why discount Tinubu's demonstrated attributes so readily in favor of Obi?

26/
In marking scripts, understanding a question, organizing arguments, analytical depth and articulation form part of assessing competence. Articulation is one observable manifestation of intelligence.

I am not suggesting automatic endorsement of Tinubu. His record and policy consequences must face the same scrutiny.
27/
Intellectual standards must be applied consistently — even when evidence challenges our preferences.

Atiku Abubakar is excluded from this comparison. Not a judgement on capacity, but he has not had direct executive responsibility governing a state.

28/
VP experience remains relevant, but comparison grounded in direct executive responsibility is more appropriate here.
The Real Measure of Leadership

The question is bigger than Obi, Tinubu or Utomi. It concerns standards by which Nigeria's intellectual community evaluates leadership — and whether applied consistently.

29/
Brilliant mind ≠ complete qualification. Good heart ≠ governance strategy. Eloquence ≠ institutional performance. Popularity ≠ transformational capacity.
Ultimate test: convert intelligence, relationships, vision and capacity into enduring institutions and measurable improvements in citizens' lives.

30/
Not who appears more gifted or appealing, but who has demonstrated ability to build institutions, develop people, sustain reforms, manage interests and turn resources into collective prosperity.

Leadership is not merely to impress with the brilliance of the officeholder. It is to translate that brilliance into collective prosperity, institutional stability and better quality of life.
That is where the conversation about Nigeria's political leadership ought to begin #NigerianPolitics #Tinubu #PeterObi #2027Elections #TinubuMustGo #Leadership

text:
The Unbeatable Checkpoint
Watch until the end this street magic crew is pure chaos. ✨

▶ Watch & continue: https://t.co/LYWAYSWXfO

#AIvideo #VideoStudio #Cuddler

Prompt:

A 30-second cinematic 3D-animated comedy short in a stylized feature-animation look with comic-book flair: soft subsurface skin shading, slightly exaggerated proportions, tactile fabric and painterly textures, subtle halftone dots and ink-line accents on fast hand moves, rich cinematic lighting. Vertical 9:16. Tone: slick, playful street-magic show, friendly rivalry, family-friendly.

THE CREW (four young adult Indonesian street magicians, all in their twenties, no costumes, no logos, each always in the same outfit):
1) THE DEALER: lanky guy, curly black mullet, gold round glasses, cream knit vest over a striped shirt, baggy grey slacks, white sneakers; long nimble fingers, a red-backed deck of cards always moving in his hand.
2) THE SHADOW: young woman, sleek black bob with blunt bangs, red lipstick, cropped black bomber jacket, high-waist cargo pants, chunky boots, thin black gloves, calm sly smile, the fastest hands of the crew.
3) THE TALKER: chubby cheerful guy, bucket hat, loud orange batik shirt, a giant plastic cup of iced coffee, a selfie stick, always grinning and talking.
4) THE YO-YO: young woman, twin braids, oversized lilac hoodie, sneakers, a glowing yo-yo on her finger.
THE CHIEF: a big, proud, middle-aged security chief with a thick moustache, crisp navy uniform, white gloves, a handheld scanner wand, and a small white robot dog at his feet. He loves his "unbeatable" checkpoint.

THE PRIZE: a thumbnail-sized glowing GOLD token. Early on it snaps magnetically onto the back of one red-backed playing card; that single gold card is the hero prop, always readable as "the card with the gold glow".

STORY: at a futuristic tech museum at night, the Chief bets the crew they can't carry the gold token through his magic-proof checkpoint: a full-body scanner arch, an X-ray tray conveyor, a red laser light curtain and his scanner wand. The crew accepts with a grin. Using pure sleight of hand and misdirection, they pass the gold card between them right under his nose — flicking it behind backs, sliding it into collars and sleeves, hiding it in a waterfall of cards, spinning it across the room. The twist: at the scanner the card isn't on any of them — it's in the Chief's own breast pocket, and the Shadow takes it back with a polite thank-you handshake.

MAGIC LANGUAGE (clear, readable hand choreography): back palm (card hidden behind the fingers), classic palm, flick-pass over the shoulder, card spring and waterfall, spinning card throw, sleeve load, quick-hands retrieval. Big obvious gestures always cover the small secret moves. Hands are anatomically correct with five fingers, moves shown in clean macro close-ups.

CAMERA LANGUAGE: "card POV" shots where the camera rides with the flying card, spinning end over end; macro inserts of fingers and the glowing token; slow motion (120 fps feel) for every pass, snapping back to real speed; whip pans that follow each throw; a 360° bullet-time orbit inside the scanner arch; crash zoom on the Chief's suspicious eyes; smooth Steadicam tracking along the queue; low-angle hero shots of the crew.

LIGHTING: cool blue-white light from the scanner arch is the main key, its rotating holographic scan rings sweeping light across faces; red show lights pulse from the ceiling; light haze makes the red laser light curtain visible as volumetric beams; the gold token is a tiny warm practical light glowing on fingers and fabric; a neon night city glitters through floor-to-ceiling windows; a polished black marble floor mirrors everything.

COLOUR: steel-blue and red palette with the gold token as the only warm accent; the final shot warms into gold.

Shot 1 (0–3s): Macro: a glowing gold token sits on a velvet pedestal under a glass dome. The Chief lifts the dome and dares the crew with a smug smile. The Dealer fans a red-backed deck over it and in one flourish the token snaps onto the back of a card. Pull back to the four magicians grinning in the blue glow. The title "S U L A P" slams on screen in bold gold block letters, then shatters into floating playing cards.
CUT TO Shot 2 (3–6s): The challenge begins: red show lights flash, the scanner arch powers up with a hum, the Chief cracks his knuckles. Steadicam tracks along the crew as they casually line up. Macro: the Dealer's hand turns over and the gold card vanishes into a back palm behind his fingers, only a thin gold glow leaking between them.
CUT TO Shot 3 (6–9s): The Chief sweeps the Dealer with the wand, arms raised. In slow motion the Dealer flicks the card over his shoulder behind his back; card POV: the camera spins with it through the red laser beams, a beam missing it by a hair; behind him the Shadow catches it between two gloved fingers without looking and slips it into her sleeve.
CUT TO Shot 4 (9–12s): The Shadow walks toward the scanner arch and fake-stumbles into the Talker; in that bump she slides the card into his batik collar. The Talker instantly creates a scene: selfie stick up, waving at the Chief, and he "accidentally" squeezes his iced coffee so ice cubes burst over the X-ray tray. Everyone looks at the mess; the X-ray screen shows only ice and a phone.
CUT TO Shot 5 (12–15s): The robot dog sniffs the Talker's ankles. The card slides down his sleeve into his palm; he performs a flashy card spring, the whole deck arcing between his hands in a waterfall, the gold card hidden inside the cascade. From the end of the waterfall he spins one card across the room: card POV, riding it through gaps in the laser curtain as it whistles over the Chief's cap.
CUT TO Shot 6 (15–18s): The Yo-Yo catches the card in the slot of her spinning yo-yo, then performs "walk the dog" along the marble floor while the Chief sweeps her with the wand. The wand beeps — tension, crash zoom on the Chief. Reveal: it beeped at his own belt buckle. She shrugs innocently and gives him a cheerful high-five and a pat on the chest; in slow motion her hand tucks the card into his breast pocket behind his name badge.
CUT TO Shot 7 (18–22s): The Chief sends all four through the full-body scanner arch together. A 360° bullet-time orbit inside the arch: blue holographic scan rings sweep up and down each magician, the floating display shows four clean silhouettes, nothing on them. Macro rack focus: the gold glow peeking out of the Chief's own breast pocket.
CUT TO Shot 8 (22–25s): The Chief grumbles and admits defeat. The Shadow offers him a warm double-handed thank-you handshake. Slow-motion macro: while he looks at her smile, her other gloved hand lifts the card out of his pocket in one smooth move; card POV as it slides up her sleeve.
CUT TO Shot 9 (25–28s): Elevator doors start to close on the four of them. The Dealer fans the deck to camera: the gold card sits in the middle, glowing. They share a quiet four-way fist bump; the Dealer blows on the fan and the whole deck bursts toward the lens, filling the frame with spinning cards.
CUT TO Shot 10 (28–30s): The cards clear to reveal the Chief alone at the checkpoint, patting his breast pocket. He pulls out a single playing card: a Joker with a hand-drawn smiley face and a tiny gold heart. His moustache twitches, then he laughs; the robot dog tilts its head. Subtitle: "Makasih ya, Pak. Tadi nitip bentar."

CONTINUITY: exactly four magicians plus the Chief, the same faces, hair and outfits in every shot; one gold token on one red-backed card, always glowing, always easy to follow; the deck is red-backed; the location is always the same blue-lit checkpoint with the red laser curtain and black marble floor.

SOUND: playful pizzicato strings and a slinky bass groove; crisp card riffles, flicks and whooshes; scanner hums and electronic beeps; ice cubes clattering; robot dog servo chirps; every slow-motion pass drops to a soft whoosh and a heartbeat, then snaps back with a riser.

AVOID: logos or readable brand names, extra on-screen text besides the title and the subtitle, more or fewer than four magicians, a second gold card, the gold card character

text:
When interviewing with Microsoft I was working as a ServiceDesk worker earning minimum wage. During the interview I was asked about my salary expectation.

At that point I had no clue what salaries in the tech industry looked like. I was also desperate to get out of the ServiceDesk/call center treadmill as it was draining me mentally.

So, I asked for a salary that was 10% higher than what I was getting.

In the end I got hired and the salary offer was 2x what I requested. God bless the salary bands for this!

Six years later I wanted to go all into software engineering. While at Microsoft I learned programming and for the last 2 years I was working mostly with ISVs, helping them to create software solutions on Microsoft Azure.

A lot of POCs, even MVPs but no real exposure to what I considered "real engineering".

Heading into the job market now I had a decent understanding on roles, salaries and while at Microsoft I think I acquired some basic negotiation skills as well. So, this time I wanted to have a proper salary negotiation.

The problem was that I was earning quite a substantial salary at Microsoft as I became quite the go-to SME within EMEA on certain areas. I was delivering internal trainings and customer trainings across all Europe.

But as a Software Engineer I was a junior.

Therefore, there wasn't any room for too much negotiation and in the end I had to accept an offer that was paying 30% less than what I was getting at Microsoft.

I still saw this as a win, because I thought going into engineering will probably be more profitable for me in the long term.

7 years later I was working at the same company and climbed up the ladder to a Technical Director role. The company was acquired by a Fortune 500 enterprise, bringing back all the corporate politics that I hoped to never face again in my life.

So, I looked for a new job.

This time I had all the cards to negotiate on my terms and I did. And I got a salary that I never thought would even be possible just 5 years prior.

Why this story?

I personally learned some things from all these experiences and I thought some of them might be useful:

- we despise salary bands, but they helped people receive offers they wouldn't ask for

- you need to understand the market and always keep the long-term in sight. Sometimes accepting a lower salary might be a good step forward

- you also need to understand your strengths and how those strengths are valued on the market.

- always understand that the salary you get when you join will represent a plateau. Most of the future increases and promotions will be negligeable

text:
@jieekusu First of all, thank you so much for your remarkable writing on Japanese pop music and its ever-evolving relationship with technology, identity, and visual culture!

I was particularly fascinated by your recent NME interview with Grimes about her collaboration with Hatsune Miku on "Miku-maxxing."

What struck me was how your conversation moved far beyond the technology itself, exploring Miku as a new kind of cultural identity—one shaped by countless creators, collective imagination, and the extraordinary possibilities of artificial pop stars.

Your writing on ATARASHII GAKKO! and other Japanese artists has also been deeply inspiring to us.

My name is THIRD PILL, founder of DREAM BABY DREAM, a Japanese music and music video label devoted entirely to generative AI and a new aesthetic we call PRINCESS POP.

Since March 2026, we have created nearly 90 original AI-generated music videos, accumulating over 15 million views on YouTube.

But what we are attempting goes far beyond the production of AI-generated content.

We believe generative AI represents the ultimate evolution of sampling culture—and perhaps the beginning of an entirely new chapter in the history of Japanese pop music.

Hatsune Miku demonstrated that a pop star no longer needed to be defined by a single human performer.

Through the creativity of thousands of producers, illustrators, animators, and fans, she became something unprecedented: a collectively imagined pop-cultural identity.

We believe generative AI is now opening another possibility.

What if we could generate not only the voice of a pop star, but the entire cinematic universe surrounding her?

The choreography, costumes, imaginary locations, visual narratives, surreal performances, and emotional landscapes that have traditionally required enormous production resources can now become part of an independent creator's artistic vocabulary.

And for us, this transformation is deeply connected to the history of pop music.

The UK's Second Summer of Love in 1988–89, Japan's Shibuya-kei movement, and the extraordinary visual and musical evolution of K-POP were all driven, in different ways, by the radical recombination of existing cultural languages.

Sampling, remixing, and editing were never merely technical procedures.

They were ways of expressing love for the past while inventing something that had never existed before.

We believe generative AI extends that creative philosophy into cinema itself.

From sampling sounds to sampling cinematic imagination.

With Seedance, we have discovered that generating moving images can feel astonishingly similar to playing electronic music—composing, remixing, improvising, and transforming visual ideas almost as if they were musical instruments.

For us, this suggests a third fundamental language in the history of moving images: after filming and drawing, generating.

Our ultimate ambition is to revive the euphoric, communal, and experimental spirit of the Second Summer of Love through Japanese idol pop, and transform it into what we call the THIRD SUMMER OF LOVE.

Yet there is a remarkable contradiction at the heart of this experiment.

Generative AI has become something of a PUBLIC ENEMY No. 1.

Our music video "Liminal Space," which brought Japanese idol pop into the uncanny world of the Backrooms, attracted an overwhelmingly international audience—and an intense controversy involving more than 1,000 critical comments.

We have repeatedly encountered accusations that AI-generated works cannot constitute genuine artistic creation.

Of course, copyright, labor, and creative ownership raise serious questions that deserve thoughtful discussion.

But we also believe that the history of pop culture has always involved challenging established definitions of authenticity, authorship, and artistic legitimacy.

From sampling to Vocaloid, from virtual idols to generative AI, each technological transformation forces us to reconsider what it means to create—and what it means to love something that may not exist in the conventional sense.

This is why your conversation with Grimes about Hatsune Miku resonated so deeply with us.

Perhaps the most exciting question is no longer whether an artificial pop star can be real, but whether the emotions, communities, and dreams that emerge around her can become something genuinely new.

Recently, Real Sound Tech published an in-depth interview about DREAM BABY DREAM, our creative philosophy, the controversy surrounding "Liminal Space," and our experiments with AI-generated pop music and cinema.

I would be deeply honored if you would consider reading it.

Given your thoughtful exploration of Japanese music, virtual identities, and the relationship between technology and pop culture, I believe our experience might offer an interesting perspective on a new creative movement emerging in Japan.

And if you ever feel that this story deserves further exploration, I would be delighted to share our work and discuss these ideas with you.

Thank you again for your inspiring writing!

DREAM BABY DREAM
THIRD PILL

text:
Elon Musk Unveils Sweeping Vision at Baron Conference: 1-Terawatt AI Chip Fab, Space Data Centers and More

Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, laid out an ambitious plan spanning in-house AI chip production, space-based AI data centers and humanoid robots in a fireside chat with Ron Baron, chairman of Baron Capital and a longtime Tesla investor.

Musk spoke with Baron for about an hour at the 33rd Annual Baron Investment Conference in New York on Nov. 6 (local time), covering Tesla and SpaceX as well as AI, semiconductors, data centers, Starlink, Starship and the future of civilization.

🔹 Terafab: "1 terawatt of AI chips a year"
Musk said today's global chipmaking capacity cannot keep up with exploding AI demand, and flagged the concentration of production in Asia, including Taiwan and Korea, as a risk. Terafab's ultimate goal is 1 terawatt (1,000 GW) of AI chip capacity per year, compared with his estimate of roughly 35–45 GW of global AI chip output next year. When Baron said it would "cost a trillion dollars," Musk replied it would be built in phases. He also aims to cut chip development cycles from a year to a month by reducing process inefficiencies.

🔹 AI revenue run-rate could top $500B by end of next year
Musk said far more companies are ordering data centers than can actually build them, calling Tesla and SpaceX's experience building giant factories and launch sites a key edge. Baron noted that conventional data centers take about two and a half years to build, while Musk's companies take eight to nine months. Musk projected the annualized revenue of SpaceX, which now includes xAI, will exceed $100B in December 2026 and could top $500B by December 2027, stressing this is "not a promise" but his best estimate.

🔹 Space AI data centers: StarMind, co-designed with NVIDIA
Musk expects AI data centers to expand into space, mainly for power: solar energy in orbit is free from atmospheric losses and far less limited by night and seasons. He said the first launches of StarMind, a space computer co-designed with NVIDIA, could begin around Q3 2027, scaling up in 2028 with large-scale deployment in 2029.

🔹 Starship & Starlink
Musk said fully reusable Starship could cut the cost of access to space by a factor of 100, with the Super Heavy booster designed to potentially re-fly once an hour. About 11,000 Starlink satellites are in orbit, and next-gen V3 satellites offer more than 10x the capability of V2, pointing to a possible 100x increase in total Starlink capacity within 2–3 years as AI agents and robots drive communication demand.

🔹 Optimus: "5x human productivity"
Musk estimated digital superintelligence alone could grow the world economy by about 20–30%, with humanoid robots adding more. He expects an Optimus robot's weekly productivity to be at least five times that of a human, and estimated 20–30 million capable robots could match the output of the entire U.S. workforce. Renting rather than selling robots was also raised as a likely model.

🔹 "A significant contribution to civilization"
Asked by the 83-year-old Baron how he hopes to be remembered at 83, Musk said he hopes he "made a significant contribution in the furtherance of civilization."

Many of the figures are projections rather than firm plans, and huge capital needs, technical hurdles and regulatory risks remain. Investors should separate Musk's vision from actual business results.

text:
We’ve all seen this frustrating cycle: a government rolls out a well-intentioned, sweeping economic intervention such as rigid price controls, one-size-fits-all industrial phase-outs, or centralized resource allocation, only for it to backfire.Because it ignored the heterogeneous needs, individual preferences, and local survival strategies of millions of ordinary people, every rigid fix ends up spawning three new problems: shortages, bottlenecks, or collateral damage to working-class livelihoods.

Faced with this dilemma, mainstream politics offers two dead ends. The Right demands that we abandon public intervention altogether and surrender to the capitalist market. The Statist Left insists that the intervention only failed because central control wasn't total enough.

From a critical, democratic socialist perspective, both miss the mark. Why do we assume "social control" must mean a handful of technocrats in a capital city designing life from above for millions of people?

The people who actually hold the vital, dispersed knowledge of how an economy functions aren't ministry planners or corporate executives. They are workers on the shop floor, tenants in neighborhoods, small farmers on the land, and local service providers. When top-down state mandates bulldoze over this practical, local knowledge , they strip society of its everyday capacity for self-adjustment and mutual aid.

Yet libertarians are equally dishonest when they claim the capitalist "free market" respects dispersed knowledge. Market prices only register preferences weighted by purchasing power, amplifying the whims of billionaires while muting the urgent needs of working-class communities. Meanwhile, multinational monopolies crush local autonomy just as ruthlessly as any state bureaucracy.

Socialism was meant to emancipate human agency, not replace the tyranny of private capital with the paternalism of the administrative state. If a left-wing project erases individual autonomy, diverse preferences, and grassroots spontaneity in the name of the collective, working people will rightly view it as a threat to the fragile ways they get by.

If we reject both corporate oligarchy and centralized bureaucratic planning, how do we build institutions through worker self-management, cooperative networks, participatory budgeting, and polycentric governance that guarantee egalitarian justice while remaining responsive to the dispersed knowledge of millions?

*Kartika Masa: The Month of Shiva and Kesava (Vishnu)..!!*

*Great sages state that there is no deity equal to Lord Vishnu, no sacred water (tirtha) equal to the River Ganga, and no month equal to the month of Kartika. Kartika Masa is especially dear to both Shiva and Kesava.*

*This month is highly sacred and spiritually potent for undertaking spiritual practices (sadhana). Every single day of this month—so beloved by both Shiva and Kesava—is considered deeply holy.*

From the *Padyami* (the first day of the lunar fortnight) to the *Purnima* (full moon day) of Kartika, people observe various *vratas* (vows/religious observances) with great devotion. Days such as *Bali Padyami* and *Bhagini Hasta Bhojanam* (a meal shared with one's sister, occurring on the second day) are considered auspicious occasions for spiritual pursuits. Offering a *deepa* (lamp)—known as *deepa daanam*—during this month yields immense spiritual merit.

*Acts of charity (*daana*), chanting (*japa*), fasting (*upavasa*), and *vana bhojanam* (communal dining in a natural/garden setting) are considered highly auspicious during Kartika Masa. Furthermore, bathing in a sacred river before sunrise, starting from the very first day of the month, is considered an act of great merit.* During the month of Kartika, it is customary to wake up before sunrise and bathe in cold water. Other significant observances during this month include lighting a lamp at dusk (*sandhya deepam*), worshipping the Tulasi plant, and performing Gauri Puja.

In the bright fortnight (*shukla paksha*) of the month of Kartika, the ninth day is known as Akshaya Navami; the eleventh day is Utthana Ekadashi; the twelfth day is Ksheerabdhi Dwadashi; and the thirteenth day is said to mark the beginning of the Svayambhuva Manvantara. The fourteenth day of this fortnight is referred to as Maha Karthi. On the full moon day (*Kartika Purnima*), the Gauri Vratam is observed, and it is a time for the *darshan* (auspicious viewing) of Lord Kartikeya. On the eleventh day of the dark fortnight (*krishna paksha*), the Bodhana Ekadashi Vratam is performed.

According to the *shastras* (scriptures), any virtuous deed performed during the month of Kartika should be dedicated to Lord Damodara (*Kartika Damodara Preetyartham*). During the autumn season (*sharad ritu*), river waters become infused with the essence of medicinal herbs. Furthermore, with the rising of the star Agastya, the pure, untainted water of this season is known as *Hamsodakam*. Bathing at dawn (*ushodaya snanam*) during the month of Kartika is highly significant, as it helps eliminate mental and physical ailments, bestowing longevity and good health; specifically, bathing in *Hamsodakam* is believed to alleviate imbalances related to *pitta* (bile/internal heat). Scholars state that bathing in a river before sunrise—with one’s body submerged up to the abdomen—can help cure abdominal ailments.

Furthermore, during the month of Kartika, singing hymns in praise of Lord Vishnu in His presence before sunrise yields the merit equivalent to donating thousands of cows. Those who play musical instruments to accompany these hymns earn the merit of performing a *Vajapeya Yajna*; those who dance earn the merit of bathing in all the sacred rivers (*Sarva Tirtha Snana*); those who offer materials for worship (*archana dravyas*) receive all these merits; and those who simply visit the temple for *darshan* receive one-sixth of these merits. Waking up at sunrise and engaging in meditation, chanting, or reciting hymns (*stotras*) dedicated to Lord Vishnu or Lord Shiva in their respective temples also grants the merit of donating thousands of cows.

text:
The Glory and Vidhi of Asvattha Pradakshinam on Somavati Amavasya.
(09-11-2026), following day after Diwali.

According to Dharmashastra, when Amavasya coincides with a Monday (Somavaram), the day attains the sacred potency of a solar eclipse (Suryagrahana-sannibhah). Any Snanam, Danam, Japam, or Shraddham performed during this rare Punyakalam yields imperishable (Akshaya) merit.

Central to this tithi is the worship and circumambulation of the sacred Peepal tree: the Asvattha Vriksha.
Svarupa of the Sacred Asvattha
In the Bhagavad Gita, Bhagavan declares: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणाम् (among all trees, I am the Asvattha).

Our Shastras reveal the divine presence enshrined within it.

 * Mula (Root): Svarupa of Brahma
 * Madhya (Trunk): Svarupa of Mahavishnu
 * Agra (Branches/Canopy): Svarupa of Parameshvara

Circumambulating the Asvattha is equivalent to seeking the combined grace of the Trimurtis and Sakala-devatas.

Pradakshinam Vidhi

 1. Sucham and Snanam - Wake up during Brahma Muhurta, take a holy bath, maintain internal and external Shuddhi, and visit an Asvattha tree.

 2. Karty (Who should observe) - Ideally, performed together as Dampatis (husband and wife). If the husband is occupied, the lady of the household can observe the vow and perform it herself.

 3. 108 Pradakshinams - The shastras prescribe completing exactly 108 Pradakshinams.

 4. Nama-Smaranam - While circumambulating, keep the mind anchored in Bhagavan-namas, stotras, or sacred shlokas.

 5. Samarpanam - Place a patra at the Mula of the tree. With each completed round (totaling 108), offer a small item.

   A. 108 sweet preparations (Bhakshanas),
   B. 108 fruits (Phalas),
   C. 108 pieces of cloth/vastram, or
   D. Coins / gold ornaments (Svarnam).
 E. Viniyogam - Upon completing all 108 rounds, distribute the offered items to devotees and the needy gathered at the kshetra.

Phalashruti

As recorded in the Bhavishyottara Puranam, Bhishma Pitamaha expounded the glory of this vrata to the Panca Pandavas in the presence of Bhagavan Shri Krishna.

Dispels bad omens, inauspicious muscle twitches (Akshi-spandanam, Bhuja-spandanam), nightmares (Duhsvapnam), and inner mental distress (Durvicitanam). Subdues hostility from adversaries (Shatru) and relieves chronic nervous and bodily ailments.

Ashirvaadam - 

Grants Sat-santanam for couples seeking children, removes impediments to marriage, and bestows Dirgha Ayus and complete Shreyas.

The Unmatched Merit of Annadanam

The Shastras place the highest premium on Annadanam under the shelter of the Asvattha on this day. Offering food, water, Majjika (buttermilk), Panakam, or varieties of cooked rice to even a single person at the base of the tree is declared to yield the Punyam equivalent to feeding one crore Brahmanas (Koti-brahmana-bhojanam).

A simple yet profound vow that protects the kula and invites divine grace.

i think one of the most dangerous things in business is becoming so busy that you forget to ask whether you're actually making progress.

you wake up, answer emails, attend meetings, check projects, solve problems and spend the entire day putting out fires.

by the end of it, you're exhausted.

and somehow, you feel productive because you barely had time to breathe.

but the interesting part is that you can spend 12 hours working on your business without doing the one thing that would actually move it forward.

maybe it's finding better customers, fixing your offer, improving your sales process or making a decision you've been avoiding for weeks.

the difference is that being busy gives you the feeling of progress without necessarily creating it.

sometimes the hardest thing for a business owner is stepping away from all the little tasks and asking what actually matters.

i guess building a business isn't about filling every hour of your day.

it's about making sure the hours you spend are taking you somewhere.

what's one thing you spend too much time on that doesn't actually move your business forward?

text:
Amelia nodded.

"I kept it because it was the last time I remember being excited about my future."

Her father sat down.

For the first time, he looked uncertain.

Then Amelia revealed something else.

She had already applied to a film production programme and received an offer.

She was leaving in six weeks.

Her mother began crying again, but this time Amelia didn't apologise.

She hugged her mother and explained that she loved her family, but she couldn't continue living a life designed by other people.

Her father didn't speak to her for several days.

Eventually, he called.

"I thought I was protecting you from making mistakes," he admitted.

Amelia replied gently, "You were protecting me from making my own choices."

She left for California the following month.

Two years later, her short film was selected for an independent film festival.

Her parents attended the screening.

After the film ended, her father approached her.

"I didn't understand your dream," he said. "But I understand now that it was yours."

Amelia hugged him.

She hadn't needed her parents to agree with every decision.

She had simply needed them to recognise that she was allowed to make one.

Sometimes, the hardest part of growing up isn't leaving home.

It's convincing the people who raised you that you are no longer a child they can plan a life for.

text:
For twenty-six years, Amelia Foster had lived a life that looked perfect to everyone except herself.

She had studied law because her parents wanted her to become a lawyer.

She had attended the university they selected, lived in the city they approved, and dated the kind of men they considered suitable.

Even her wedding plans had once been discussed before she was old enough to understand what marriage meant.

Her parents called it guidance.

Amelia called it a lifetime of decisions made without her permission.

The breaking point came when her father announced that she would be leaving her job in Denver to join the family law firm.

He had already spoken to his business partners.

He expected her to start the following month.

Amelia refused.

Her father was furious.

"After everything we've done for you, this is how you repay us?"

Her mother began crying.

"Your father only wants the best for you."

Amelia finally lost control.

"Have either of you ever asked what I want?"

The room went silent.

She continued.

"You chose my school. You chose my course. You chose my friends. You even tried to choose the person I would marry. Every time I disagreed, you reminded me how much you sacrificed to raise me."

Her father interrupted.

"We sacrificed because we wanted you to have a good life!"

Amelia looked at him.

"Then why have I never been allowed to live it?"

She went upstairs and returned with an old envelope.

Inside were university application forms she had secretly completed when she was eighteen.

She had wanted to study filmmaking.

She had received an offer from a university in California but never attended because her parents insisted she study law.

For years, she had kept the acceptance letter.

Her mother recognised it immediately.

"You still have that?"

text:
Atlas being free is nice, but don't fall into this trap because: 

Atlas being free is nice, but this could turn out to be a trap for you if you don't know the cost of maintaining one. Here is this-

? Delaware tax: $400/yr for an LLC (was $300 till this year), due June 1. Late adds $200 plus 1.5% a month

? C corp instead? Franchise tax + annual report by March 1. Min $175 if you use the right method. Use the default and some founders get a bill in the thousands

? Registered agent, every year, LLC or C corp

? Form 1120 for a C corp, even at zero revenue

? Form 5472 if you're foreign-owned and money moved between you and the company. Your first wire to fund the account counts. Miss it and it's a $25K penalty

? 83(b) election if your founder shares vest. 30 days from issuance, no extensions. Miss it and you may pay tax on growth later

? Operating from another US state? You may need to register there too. California alone is $800/yr minimum

Bookkeeping. You can't file any of the above with a messy ledger and read the fine print on the free offer. 

Incorporating is easy. Staying compliant is where the bills are.

Breaking: Bangladesh Air Force to Acquire 20 J-10CE Fighter Jets from China in a $1.96 Billion Deal

Zahed-ur-Rahman, an advisor to the Bangladeshi government, has confirmed to the media that the policy and financial approvals for the Bangladesh Air Force’s procurement of 20 Chinese-made J-10CE fighter jets have been finalized.

The Bangladeshi Ministry of Finance has authorized a state guarantee to finance the J-10CE acquisition. The principal cost for the aircraft is approximately $1.96 billion, with an additional $170 million in interest, bringing the total value to roughly $2.1316 billion. An initial payment of $391.9 million is required, and the first aircraft is scheduled for delivery in 2027.

With an exceptional price-to-performance ratio—averaging $98 million per aircraft—and a proven combat record (notably including the reported downing of several Rafale fighters during aerial engagements between Pakistan and India), this Chinese "4.5-generation" fighter has become increasingly attractive. Beyond Bangladesh, Uzbekistan has already ordered 24 J-10CEs, while countries such as Indonesia, Egypt, Serbia, and Azerbaijan have also shown significant interest.

The J-10CE is a medium-weight, 4.5-generation fighter equipped with an Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) fire-control radar, advanced onboard electronic warfare systems, a joint helmet-mounted cueing system, a variety of sophisticated air-to-air missiles, and precision-guided munitions. At a cost of less than $100 million per unit, it arguably offers the best value for money of any medium-weight, 4.5-generation fighter currently on the global market.

For comparison, the contracts signed by India, Indonesia, and France for the Rafale fighter carry an average price tag exceeding $250 million per aircraft, while the Swedish Saab JAS-39E/F fighters procured by the Royal Thai Air Force cost over $150 million each.

This highlights how the Western military-industrial complex generates massive profits—often while attaching stringent political conditions to their defense exports.
