🌐 The Legacy of Hope : 

How NTR Garu, The NTR Trust, and Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu built a World class Cancer Care Hospital in Hyderabad .

Great institutions are rarely born out of convenience; they are forged in the crucible of personal grief and transformed into public missions.

The story of the Basavatarakam Indo-American Cancer Hospital & Research Institute (BIACH&RI) in Hyderabad is a masterclass in how political will, philanthropic execution, and global medical expertise can converge to change the healthcare landscape of a nation. 

Here is the untold depth behind this monumental institution. 👇

1. The Catalyst: NTR’s Personal Grief & Vision

In the mid-1980s, the legendary matinée idol and former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao (NTR), faced a devastating personal tragedy. His wife, Smt. Nandamuri Basavatarakam, tragically succumbed to cancer. During her battle, NTR realized a painful truth: world-class cancer treatment was a luxury reserved only for those who could afford to travel abroad. 

Before her passing, Smt. Basavatarakam expressed a profound wish—that no family should have to endure the agony of losing a loved one simply because they couldn't afford therapy.

Driven by this promise, NTR setup the Smt. Nandamuri Basavataraka Rama Rao Memorial Cancer Foundation (NBTRCF). He envisioned a state-of-the-art facility in Hyderabad that would offer world-class oncology care on a not-for-profit basis, proving that quality treatment is a fundamental human right, not a privilege. 

2. The Anchor: The NTR Trust & Sustained Philanthropy

While NTR laid the foundation, executing a project of this scale required sustained structural backing. This is where the Nandamuri family, under the leadership of Trust Chairman Shri Nandamuri Balakrishna, stepped in to scale the mission. 

The Not-for-Profit Model : 

The hospital operates seamlessly on a cross-subsidy structure. Revenue generated from those who can afford care directly funds the treatment of underprivileged patients. 

Unprecedented Growth: 
What started as a focused dream has transformed into a massive 500+ bed ultra-modern facility. 

Holistic Innovation: 
Beyond conventional oncology, the trust uniquely integrated a Center for Alternative Medicine (offering Naturopathy and Ayurveda) alongside cutting-edge diagnostic setups like the recently launched Digital Pathology facilities. 

3. The Medical Architect: Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu

A hospital needs walls, but a medical institution needs a soul and international stature. 

Enter Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, a globally acclaimed radiation oncologist who journeyed from a small village in Krishna district , Andhra Pradesh to Manhattan, USA

Dr. Nori, who served as the Chief of Brachytherapy at the prestigious Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Director at New York-Presbyterian Hospital, was instrumental from day one. 

The Global Connection: Dr. Nori co-founded the Indo-American Cancer Organization (IACO) in the USA, linking global oncology breakthroughs directly to Hyderabad. 

Strategic Advisory: As a long-standing Board Member and official Cancer Care Advisor to the Telugu states, Dr. Nori designs the roadmap for modernizing the hospital's clinical protocols. 

Accolades of Excellence: In recognition of his massive contributions to global oncology and his selfless service to India, the Government of India honored him with the Padma Shri (2015) and the prestigious Padma Bhushan (2026). 

4. The Impact Today

Inaugurated in June 2000 by the late Prime Minister Sri Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Basavatarakam has recently marked 25 years of compassionate care. It stands consistently rated among the absolute best cancer care hospitals in India. 

Today, Dr. Nori is leading a major public health roadmap through the institution, actively aiming to entirely eradicate certain preventable cancers in the region within the next six to seven years through aggressive public awareness and early screening.

Dr Nori Dattatreyudu is also a recipient of the Prestigious Padma Sri and Padma Vibhushan awards.

The convergence of NTR's unmatched political will, the relentless execution of the NTR Trust foundations, and Dr. Nori’s clinical brilliance created a sanctuary of healing that continues to save thousands of lives daily.

text:
Crypto industry wins 245 supporters in Congress with $176 million, but loses allies in key committees. Crypto Recap No. 170  
Week 46, November 2–8, 2026

Cryptocurrencies closed in the red. The past week in the crypto market was shaped by outside forces: law enforcement, voters, and regulators. The Binance hack is being investigated by the FBI, while supervisory authorities are checking whether American banks could withstand such an attack. The industry poured money into campaigns for its allies, but both chambers of Congress shifted to the Democrats. Meanwhile, regulated exchanges in the US and Russia are adopting crypto assets and crypto-exchange instruments, but trading conditions on them are set by regulators and issuers.

Crypto hacks are becoming a matter for states  
The largest hack in cryptocurrency history has become the subject of a state dispute and banking supervision checks. The FBI accused North Korea of stealing $6.3 billion from Binance and demanded that companies block addresses linked to the hackers. Kim Jong Un’s sister called the accusations political. In 2026, Binance blocked 57 potential threats from North Korean hackers. According to the exchange, the successful attack lasted five months: using fake job interviews, the hackers infiltrated the employee database, and malicious AI gave them access to the internal signing of wallets. The exchange compensated 95% of the stolen funds, allocating 7,500 BTC ($583 million) from its SAFU reserve fund for this purpose. According to Reuters, the Federal Reserve and the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) are checking American banks’ systems for vulnerabilities.

The crypto industry loses allies at the helm of congressional committees  
The industry’s election money did not keep its allies in committee chairmanships. Crypto super PACs spent more than $176 million on the midterm elections, mainly backing Republicans, but Democrats won majorities in both chambers. Among those elected are 245 crypto supporters, up from more than 200 after the previous elections. The Senate Banking Committee may instead be chaired by industry critic Elizabeth Warren rather than Republican Tim Scott. French Hill, the sponsor of the CLARITY bill, will lose his post as chairman of the House Financial Services Committee starting in January 2027. The main contenders for his seat are crypto opponents Maxine Waters and Sean Casten. After the Binance hack, Waters accused Republicans of weakening oversight and is preparing a bill on crypto market structure that would expand the powers of the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The stock market is adopting crypto on its own terms  
The line between the crypto and stock markets is blurring, but under stock market rules. On November 3, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved trading in perpetual futures on US stocks after applications from Coinbase, Kalshi, and Payward, Kraken’s parent company. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said such contracts may be offered on exchanges registered with both the SEC and the CFTC. Moscow Exchange will launch trading in BTC, ETH, and USDT on December 1 using stock market technology. After completing a test, retail investors will be able to invest up to 300,000 rubles ($3,700) per year through a single broker. Fifty-six of the 62 companies, including SpaceX, Tesla, and Amazon, have already opposed the tokenization of their shares on the OKX-ICE platform.

This is Eric Hartford’s Wizard Vicuna 7B Uncensored in a widely used quantized distribution. Pick a Q4 or Q5 GGUF supported by your runner and start with a short context. Keep any local API bound only to the interface you need.

The entry lists “Other; check original and quantizer terms.” Verify the original model terms and the quantizer’s license before redistribution or commercial use. This is an older uncensored model, so apply human review, input controls and output filtering. text:
Sjoe! The AI Revolution Has Arrived⚡ Eskom Is Still Looking for the Extension Cord! ~ 🚰 Silicon Valley Wants Data Centres. South Africa Can't Even Deliver the Water for the Cooling System! ~ We've Got the Memorandum, the Partnership and the Photo Opportunity🎤 Anyone Got a Working Generator?
The numbers arrived first and they were not subtle. In 2026 the four largest American hyperscalers guided capital expenditure of roughly $720–740 billion. Broader trackers that included related players placed the figure near or above $800 billion. Quarterly run-rates exceeded $200 billion. 

Independent estimates credited this spending with a material share—up to two-thirds under wider definitions—of recent United States real GDP growth. 

Power, water and specialised chips had become the binding constraints on the largest peacetime capital concentration in living memory.

Against that benchmark South Africa recorded real GDP growth averaging near 1 percent for much of the period after 2010, youth unemployment near 47 percent, non-revenue water losses stabilised at roughly 47 percent of treated supply, and foreign holdings of rand government bonds still material at 24–26 percent. 

The same variable that attracted record capital elsewhere—uninterrupted electrons and water—had been missing at home for fifteen years. Reliability had ceased to be an engineering problem. It had become the decisive strategic constraint. 

Everything else—non-alignment, partnership announcements, fiscal space, industrial ambition—now resolved to that single test.

1. The Scale That Moves the Dial

Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta did not invent the demand for reliable infrastructure; they simply priced it at a level that could not be ignored. Their combined 2026 guidance sat between $720 billion and $740 billion. Some trackers pushed the broader group past $800 billion. Year-on-year growth in several quarters approached 80–100 percent. 

A National Bureau of Economic Research working paper observed that the projected multi-year AI build-out would absorb a higher share of GDP than the American railroad expansion of the late nineteenth century, and would do so in a shorter time. 

Power availability, grid connections and specialised chip supply emerged as the hard limits. Free cash flow at several of the firms turned negative, shifting financing toward debt markets.

The capital was not searching first for cheap labour or generous tax holidays. It was searching for places where the lights stayed on and the cooling water arrived on schedule. Secondary effects on energy demand, construction employment and fiscal multipliers became macro-relevant in the United States precisely because the physical systems could absorb the load. 

Historical infrastructure waves—railroads, electrification, the interstate highway system—had always privileged locations that could deliver continuity. The current wave simply compressed the timeline and raised the price of failure. Institutional incentives reinforced the pattern. 

Hyperscalers face continuous competitive pressure to secure capacity ahead of rivals. Delay is expensive. Jurisdictions that cannot guarantee uptime are simply crossed off the shortlist. 

The market does not negotiate with load-whatever they want to call it now schedules.

Sjoe.
A country that still treats reliable electricity as a negotiable aspiration has already priced itself out of the conversation, no matter how many investment conferences it hosts.

Questions Stirring:
If capital of this magnitude now prices reliability above almost every other variable, what remaining advantage can an economy claim when its own systems fail the basic test? 
Does the historical parallel with earlier infrastructure waves raise the question of whether latecomers can still catch the curve, or does the speed of the current wave close the window faster than previous cycles? 
Why do public statements continue to celebrate announced investment while the binding constraint—continuous power and water—remains unaddressed?

What these questions together reveal is a shift in the terms of industrial competition. They force attention away from the volume of capital elsewhere and onto the operational precondition that decides whether any of it can land. Without that precondition the rest of the conversation becomes theatre.

2. The Portfolio’s Quiet Counterweight

Even the winners of the capital wave required insurance. Concentrated technology equity exposures embed optimistic assumptions about sustained growth and margins. When those assumptions weaken—through slower adoption, higher costs or valuation resets—the negative correlation between equities and high-quality bonds typically reasserts itself. 

Duration delivers price gains as yields fall in risk-off episodes. Historical episodes of technology-led concentration, from the late 1990s to the early 2020s, showed bonds cushioning equity drawdowns more consistently than commodities or cash.

Corporate issuance linked to AI projects can increase supply, yet the core hedging logic remains the flight-to-safety channel. Portfolio construction that ignores this channel leaves investors exposed to correlated downside in the very sector driving recent returns. 

The appeal of bonds persists across interest-rate regimes because the risk being hedged is growth and valuation risk, not solely inflation risk.

The deeper institutional point is asymmetry. Sophisticated capital still insists on a reliable offset. An economy whose own sovereign instruments are themselves fragile has fewer such offsets available when external conditions tighten. 

Domestic banks and pension funds already carry heavy sovereign exposure. Any further pressure on the bond market therefore transmits quickly into the broader financial system.

Sjoe.
Even the winners keep a parachute. The question is what happens to an economy that never packed one.

Questions Stirring:
If the largest technology firms still require high-quality duration as a hedge, what does that imply for a sovereign whose own debt market is already heavily owned by domestic institutions? 
Does the persistence of the stock-bond correlation across cycles raise the question of whether fiscal vulnerability can ever be insulated from global technology shocks? 
Why is the domestic debate still framed around attracting equity capital when the first line of defence for that capital is the bond market itself?

What these questions together reveal is the link between external capital waves and internal instruments of risk management. Fragility at home is not merely a growth problem. It is a balance-sheet problem that surfaces the moment global risk appetite shifts.

3. The Domestic Arithmetic of Unreliability

South Africa’s record supplied the contrast with clinical clarity. Real GDP growth averaged near 1 percent for much of the period after 2010. Per-capita income stagnated or declined after 2013. Official unemployment remained in the low-to-mid 30 percent range; youth unemployment hovered near 47 percent in recent quarters. 

Severe load-shedding in 2022–2023 subtracted an estimated 1–3 percentage points from annual growth in peak years and imposed cumulative costs measured in hundreds of billions of rand. Non-revenue water losses stabilised near 47 percent of treated supply, a physical and fiscal leakage of roughly R26 billion annually according to official figures. 

Manufacturing’s contribution to GDP continued its long decline. Foreign direct investment conversion rates stayed weak; less than half of announced commitments materialised in recent cycles.

The numbers are not contested. They appear in Statistics South Africa releases, World Bank updates and National Treasury documents. What they demonstrate is that the physical preconditions for participation in power- and water-intensive global industries were systematically absent. 

Capital that can choose between locations will not choose the location where the cooling system fails or the voltage drops.

Political science offers a useful lens. Short electoral cycles reward visible announcements more than the slow work of system maintenance. Cadre deployment patterns and procurement weaknesses, long documented in governance inquiries, reduce the capacity to insist on genuine performance. 

The result is not conspiracy. It is the predictable outcome of constrained institutions meeting capital that can deliver scale elsewhere.

International comparisons sharpen the point. Economies that successfully moved from mineral dependence to manufacturing depth did so by treating reliability as non-negotiable. 

South Africa’s own automotive sector under preferential arrangements once demonstrated that higher-value exports are possible when commercial terms reward local content and skills. 

The same logic has not yet been applied at scale to the broader minerals-to-metals chain or to the energy system that underpins it.

Sjoe.
Fifteen years of measured underperformance produced a simple operational result: the country was not on the shortlist for the largest capital wave of the decade. The spreadsheets noticed before the speeches did.

Questions Stirring:
If the growth, unemployment and infrastructure numbers have been public for years, what additional evidence would be required before the political system treats them as binding rather than aspirational? 
Does the persistence of 47 percent non-revenue water and 47 percent youth unemployment raise the question of whether any external partnership can compensate for domestic system failure? 
Why do successive investment pledges continue to outrun the conversion rate into actual projects?

What these questions together reveal is the conversion of a long statistical record into a single operational diagnosis. Without reliability the rest of the industrial conversation is theatre, and theatre does not keep furnaces lit.

4. The Fiscal Transmission Mechanism

Foreign investors still hold roughly 24–26 percent of rand-denominated government bonds, down from peaks above 40 percent but still material. A credible restriction or strong discouragement of United States purchases would raise yields, increase debt-service costs and force greater absorption by domestic banks and pension funds already heavily exposed to sovereign debt. 

Fiscal space for infrastructure rehabilitation and employment programmes would shrink precisely when both are most needed. Secondary effects—rand pressure, higher import costs, elevated risk premia across the curve—would compound the original constraint. 

Allied jurisdictions and global asset managers frequently adjust exposure in response to United States capital-market signals, amplifying the initial impact beyond direct holdings.

Economists have publicly identified this channel as more potent than trade measures alone. The result would be a tighter fiscal constraint layered on top of systems that already fail the reliability test. 

Unreliability is therefore not only an operational cost; it is a sovereign balance-sheet risk.

The constitutional implication is rarely stated. Socio-economic rights presuppose material capacity. A state that cannot keep the lights on or the water flowing cannot meaningfully deliver those rights at scale. 

Treating the grid and the municipal water system as sites of political contest rather than load-bearing foundations therefore undermines the very rights the contest claims to advance.

Sjoe.
When the bond market becomes the last institution still insisting that two plus two equals four, the political system has already outsourced arithmetic.

Questions Stirring:
If foreign bond holdings remain material, does a shift in United States appetite raise the question of how quickly domestic institutions can absorb the difference without crowding out private credit? 
What measurable improvement in power and water reliability would be required before the risk premium on sovereign debt begins to compress? 
Why is the public debate still focused on trade preferences when the capital-market channel carries larger and faster fiscal consequences?

What these questions together reveal is how domestic system failure transmits into the instruments that finance the state itself. The cost of unreliability is no longer confined to the factory floor. It appears on the national balance sheet.

5. Layered Risk and the Search for a Third Vector

Additional layers compound the surface. Coercive networks in transport, construction and informal mining raise project costs where formal order is weak. Informal remittance flows estimated at R6.3 billion in one metro study combine capital leakage that reduces local employment multipliers with residual terrorist-financing risk flags under international frameworks. 

MTN’s disclosed United States Department of Justice scrutiny of historical Iran and Afghanistan operations, together with ongoing Anti-Terrorism Act civil cases, adds corporate-level legal and reputational exposure under United States statutes.

Against this multi-layered surface an existing Japanese industrial relationship—Toyota-scale automotive process discipline and JICA-supported water-sector technical cooperation—offers a non-binary pathway into intermediate manufacturing steps such as materials processing or advanced packaging. 

Japan’s own lithography equipment makers and semiconductor revival efforts create a potential technology vector that is less binary than pure United States–China alignment. The pathway remains contingent, however, on the same domestic reliability deficit that has been missing for fifteen years. 

Without continuous power and water, even the most promising external platform stays aspirational.

The water-sector experience supplies something rarer than any single technology: a demonstrated sequence. Memorandum of cooperation, joint technical design, construction of local training infrastructure, training-of-trainers, sustained official exchanges. 

That sequence has already been walked from agreement to physical facility. Implementation has been imperfect and national outcomes remain incomplete, yet the institutional pathway is visible. 

The rational next step is systematic extension rather than perpetual reinvention.

Sjoe.
It is always tempting to treat a promising foreign technology and a domestic mineral endowment as if they were already a joint industrial strategy. The distance between the two is measured in capital, skills, yield learning and market access—not in press releases.

Questions Stirring:
If coercive networks and informal capital leakage already raise the cost of formal projects, what additional institutional reforms would be required before a Japanese-mediated manufacturing step becomes commercially viable? 
Does the existence of a working technical-cooperation method in the water sector raise the question of why that method has not been systematically extended to industrial skills and process discipline? 
Why does the public conversation still leap to “chip fab” when the more plausible near-term opportunities lie several steps earlier in the value chain?

What these questions together reveal is the necessity of sequence. They keep ambition tethered to intermediate steps and prevent the mineral advantage and the technology discussion from being rhetorically fused into an illusion of readiness.

Synthesis

The independent lines of evidence converge with unusual clarity. 
Record hyperscaler capital expenditure prices reliability above almost every other variable. 
Sophisticated portfolio construction still insists on high-quality bonds as the primary hedge. 
South Africa’s fifteen-year growth, unemployment and infrastructure record demonstrates the cost of failing the reliability test. 
Foreign bond holdings transmit that failure into fiscal space. Layered domestic risks amplify external vulnerability, while the only concrete alternative partnership remains contingent on the same missing foundation.

The argument is falsifiable. Measurable, sustained improvement in power availability and non-revenue water, rising conversion rates of announced investment into operating projects, and a declining risk premium on sovereign debt would alter the picture. 

Until those numbers move, the operational diagnosis holds. Reliability is no longer a downstream engineering problem. It is the primary strategic constraint.

Multiple camera angles now describe the same scene. Capital markets, national accounts, infrastructure statistics and corporate disclosures all point in one direction. The rope is stronger than any single strand.

Objections

One objection holds that any large external market is better than none and that mineral demand itself sustains the economy. Foreign-exchange inflows matter. Yet the same inflows have accompanied the contraction of manufacturing capacity and the persistence of infrastructure failure, showing that volume alone does not restore competitive cost structures.

A second objection insists that localisation targets and partnership announcements already protect sovereignty. The targets exist. Independent verification of equity depth, technology transfer and offtake independence remains sparse, and capacity continues to shrink.

A third objection claims that domestic failures are separate from external relationships. The failures are domestic in origin, yet they determine how every external relationship is experienced—as opportunity or as multiplier of cost.

Each objection is testable. None yet overturns the cumulative pattern.

Conclusion

The five sections resolve to a single operational truth. In an era when industrial power is measured by the ability to keep electrons and capital flowing without interruption, a middle-income economy whose most basic systems remain unreliable cannot participate on equal terms, no matter how many diplomatic postures it adopts or partnership memoranda it signs. 

South Africa’s published numbers already supply the argument. The remaining question is whether the political system can treat those numbers as binding rather than aspirational.

Any credible industrial strategy—Japan-mediated or otherwise—begins with the unglamorous work of restoring the systems that make capital and skills productive. 

Without that foundation, non-alignment is residual rather than chosen, and partnership remains a press release. The capital wave has already priced the variable. 

The only open question is whether the country will.

Sjoe.
The most radical act left may be the quiet decision to treat reality as real and then get back to work.

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/SOx3zZGAdb | Author: @militarnyi Argentina to Acquire Four Black Hawk Helicopters for $28 Million, Down from Approved $140 Million 
Argentina has signed a $28 million deal with the United States to purchase four UH-60L Black Hawk multirole helicopters for its Army Aviation Corps.

Argentina’s Ministry of Defense announced the agreement.

The Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) was signed on November 6 by Argentine Defense Minister Carlos Alberto Presti, U.S.Ambassador Peter Lamelas, and senior Argentine military officials.

Argentina is acquiring the helicopters through the U.S. Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program, using the Black Hawk Exchange and Sales Transaction (BEST) initiative.

According to Argentina’s Ministry of Defense, Argentine officials negotiated a price of approximately $28 million for the first four helicopters. The deal also includes spare parts and consumables.

 U.S. Ambassador Peter Lamelas and representatives of Argentina’s military leadership. November 6, 2026. Photo credits: Argentina’s Ministry of Defense

The first UH-60L Black Hawk is expected to arrive in Argentina by the end of 2026. The four helicopters will form the initial fleet of this type operated by the country’s Army Aviation Corps.

On September 10, the U.S. State Department approved the potential sale of four UH-60L Black Hawk helicopters and related equipment to Argentina for up to $140 million.

The initial package included two additional T700-GE-701D engines, navigation and communication equipment, spare parts, personnel training, and technical support.

The $140 million figure represented the maximum estimated value of the proposed sale, not the final cost of the signed agreement.

 UH-60L Black Hawk. Photo credits: Portuguese Air Force

Black Hawk Helicopters for Argentina

The UH-60L Black Hawk can carry up to 11 troops and reach about 280 km/h, depending on payload and flight conditions.

The helicopters are powered by two T700-GE-701D turboshaft engines and feature digital avionics, a Garmin GTN 750navigation system, and multiband communications equipment.

For special operations, the helicopters will be equipped with a Fast Rope Insertion and Extraction System (FRIES) and an external cargo hook. They are also configured to use a Bambi Bucket underslung firefighting system for aerial firefighting operations.

The new helicopters will serve the Argentine Army in a range of missions, including rapid troop deployment, cargo transport, search and rescue operations, and emergency response.

To prepare pilots and maintenance personnel, the Argentine military has already sent representatives to Colombia, which has extensive experience operating Black Hawk helicopters.

 A U.S. Army UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter during an exercise in Okinawa, Japan. October 27, 2020. Photo credits: Elias M.Chelala / U.S. Army

On November 7, Latvia received the last of four UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters ordered from the United States. The aircraft are replacing the country’s Soviet-era Mi-17 helicopters.

In September, Militarnyi reported that Argentina was planning to secure $3.5 billion in loans to purchase three submarines and two frigates as part of its naval modernization program.

Atlas being free is nice, but this could turn out to be a trap for you if you don't know the cost of maintaining one. 

Here is this why? 

? Delaware tax: $400/yr for an LLC (was $300 till this year), due June 1. Late adds $200 plus 1.5% a month

? C corp instead? Franchise tax + annual report by March 1. Min $175 if you use the right method. Use the default and some founders get a bill in the thousands

? Registered agent, every year, LLC or C corp

? Form 1120 for a C corp, even at zero revenue

? Form 5472 if you're foreign-owned and money moved between you and the company. Your first wire to fund the account counts. Miss it and it's a $25K penalty

? 83(b) election if your founder shares vest. 30 days from issuance, no extensions. Miss it and you may pay tax on growth later

? Operating from another US state? You may need to register there too. California alone is $800/yr minimum

Bookkeeping. You can't file any of the above with a messy ledger and read the fine print on the free offer. 

Incorporating is easy. Staying compliant is where the bills are.

PS: incorporate not because it's free, incorporate because it makes sense for you

#Trump Appoints #Miller White House Chief of Staff Following Loss of #Congress, Signals Shift to Hardline Stance

Donald Trump has appointed 41-year-old Stephen Miller as White House Chief of Staff immediately following the Republicans' defeat in the midterm elections and the loss of control over both houses of Congress. The appointment was announced on November 6 and takes effect on November 9. Miller will replace Susie #Wiles, who is being transferred to the president's political team. Instead of a negotiator, Trump has placed one of the most uncompromising ideologues of his platform at the helm of the administration, prepared to confront Democrats, tighten immigration restrictions, and leverage executive powers without congressional backing. Reports indicate this, citing #Reuters.

Miller has worked alongside Trump since the 2016 presidential campaign, serving in both administrations and overseeing the drafting of executive orders. The president called him one of his most trusted advisors. In contrast to Wiles, who was known for her ability to negotiate with politicians and business leaders, Miller advocates for the aggressive application of executive authority. Sources cited by Reuters expect an expanded use of presidential decrees, intensified pressure on congressional Republicans, and a refusal to make significant concessions to Democrats.

The primary priority remains the continuation of mass deportations despite declining public support. An October Reuters/#Ipsos poll showed that only 37% of Americans approved of Trump's immigration policies, down from 50% at the start of his presidential term. Four immigration agency officials confirmed to the news agency that there are no signs of easing enforcement: established arrest quotas remain in effect.

Republicans had warned Miller about the political fallout prior to the elections. Nebraska Congressman Don #Bacon revealed that lawmakers pointed to voter dissatisfaction over deportations and tariffs, but Miller rejected their arguments. Following the party's defeat, Bacon characterized Miller's appointment as doubling down on a failed strategy and reported a sharply negative reaction among members of Congress.

Miller now faces the task of preventing Republicans from distancing themselves from the president amid upcoming investigations by the Democratic-led Congress. Strategist Ron #Bonjean warned that any attempts by lawmakers to step away from the administration would meet fierce resistance. Trump donor and energy executive Dan #Eberhart described the new strategy as a "bunker defense" for the remaining two years. Presidential ally Roger #Stone referred to Miller as Trump's "wartime consigliere."

Miller's influence will also extend to foreign policy. Three sources told Reuters that he opposes drawing out the war with #Iran while remaining a firm supporter of #Israel. These positions could complicate dynamics within the administration: Trump has previously threatened to resume strikes against Iran and announced a suspension of aid to Israel.

Corporate lobbyists also anticipate a hardening of the White House line. Unlike Wiles, who maintained active communication with top business executives, Miller is focused on immigration, tariffs, and political battles. Business representatives fear diminished opportunities to influence the administration's economic policy decisions.

Following the elections, Trump has already directed the Justice Department to investigate Democrats whom he accused of threatening Republican donors and allies. Simultaneously, the president offered the post of White House Press Secretary to #UFC CEO Dana #White. As Congress transitions to Democratic control, the administration is not softening its posture, but rather concentrating power around the president's closest ideological ally. Miller assumes leadership of the White House ahead of two years of intense political clashes, congressional investigations, and the battle to preserve Trump's leverage.

text:
Zano Ecosystem Recap: November 1–8, 2026

Activity this week centered on in-person events (AIBC World in Rome and Exit and Build 6), the release of the September–October Monthly Project Update, continued promotion of real-world spending tools, and steady messaging around ZanoNames, privacy, and permissionless options.

Official and partner posts emphasized practical usability, recovery progress, and partnership conversations, while core development priorities remained consistent.

1/ Events & Partnerships

The week was defined by conferences.

Zano maintained a booth (H7-7381) at AIBC World in Rome (November 2–5). On November 3 the team invited visitors interested in private payments or the broader ecosystem.

The wrap-up post on November 7 noted productive catch-ups with existing partners @AEON_Community and @AlchemyPay, plus new conversations with @BasicSwapDEX, @0Xprocessing, and other payment processors and custody providers. The team returned to building afterward.

Exit and Build 6 (November 5–8 at Sovereignty Ranch, Bandera, Texas) ran in parallel.

Zano sponsored the event; @SallyMayweather represented the project with a talk on why private and permissionless money belongs among tools for parallel systems (local food, trade, networks, etc.).

2/ Monthly Project Update & Development Focus

On November 5, @zano_project published the Monthly Project Update #24 covering September and October. Key points included:

• Details of the HF7 recovery after the Gateway Addresses vulnerability (unauthorized minting of ZANO and fUSD; no user funds or privacy compromised). Gateway Addresses remain disabled pending an independent audit.

• New/maintenance releases for the desktop wallet, Lite Wallet, and Companion extension.

• @ZanoNames marketplace for tradable Zano aliases (still "coming soon").

• BTCPay Server plugin testing and ZEL (Zano Execution Layer) testnet progress.

• Coverage of the Rome and Texas events.

Public messaging continued to highlight the same three priorities, with no major new technical milestones or audit completion announced this week:

• Completing the independent Gateway Addresses audit (required before re-enabling the feature and advancing integrations such as THORChain).

• Building the Zano Execution Layer (ZEL) for EVM-compatible smart contracts and programmability around Confidential Assets.

• Progress toward Zenith (full Proof-of-Stake with hidden amounts, targeting faster blocks and finality).

3/ Real-World Spending & Usability

Practical spending options stayed in focus.

On November 4, @zano_project reminded users they can load zano:native or $FUSD onto Zebec debit cards (@ZebecCards) and spend them anywhere Mastercard is accepted—no top-up fee, settlement in USD or EUR, and support for Apple Pay / Google Pay.

On November 8 the account highlighted zano:native availability in Freedom Wallet, pairing self-custody ("holding your own keys") with private money that cannot be censored or frozen.

AEON Pay support for loading ZANO/fUSD and spending at tens of millions of local merchants (Nigeria, Vietnam, Philippines, and other markets) remained part of the broader narrative, building on earlier integrations.

4/ Aliases & ZanoNames

@ZanoNames continued promoting the upcoming marketplace for tradable Zano aliases (fixed-price listings, auctions, and escrow-backed trades verified on-chain, payable in ZANO or fUSD).

Messaging emphasized ownership, transferability, utility for payments and dApp sign-ins, and the idea that rare or culturally relevant names can become valuable assets.

Launch timing was still described as approaching, consistent with the late-October announcement and the monthly update.

5/ Privacy Education, Partners & Community

• Freedom Dollar (@freedomdollar5) kept posting USDT freeze alerts on Tron (contrasting centralized stablecoins that can freeze balances with fUSD, which has no admin keys or blacklist capability). It also announced that XMR ↔ fUSD swaps are now live on Freedom Swap with low fees in both directions.

• Zano Africa (@ZanoAfrica) amplified the monthly update and Rome activity for the African community.

• ZanoX (@ZanoX_io) posted on the combination of self-custody and privacy.

• Community accounts shared weekly-style recaps highlighting recovery transparency, wallet work, integrations, and real-world payments.

A Privacy Roundtable X Space featuring @GinoFPM (Head of Community) from Zano was scheduled for November 10.

6/ Market

zano:native showed volatility with a mid-week recovery.

It opened near roughly $3.80–$3.86 on November 1 (market cap in the mid-to-high $50M range) and saw a dip toward the low $3s before rebounding strongly around November 4–5 (intraday highs near $5 in some data).

It closed the period in the low-to-mid $4s (market cap generally $60–75M range depending on the source and day). Daily volumes on tracked venues typically stayed in the $0.6–1.5M range.

Looking Ahead

Near-term focus remains completing the Gateway Addresses independent audit (to unlock re-enablement and broader permissionless integrations such as THORChain), continued ZEL and Zenith work, the ZanoNames launch, pending wallet/Companion/BTCPay releases, and further real-world payment options.

The Privacy Roundtable on November 10 offers an upcoming public update opportunity.

Plot Overview: Frederick Alvin Davis II rises above the limitations of the Antebellum era, graduating from Harvard University Law School. His leadership skills shine during the Civil War, where he commands an All-Antebellum-Black American regiment, earning acclaim for his battlefield victories. His success catches the attention of President Abraham Lincoln, with whom he shares not only a profession, they both stood 6'4" and also a vision for a better America. Davis becomes a trusted aide in Lincoln's cabinet and later a U.S. Senator for North Carolina. Frederick Alvin Davis II had a considerable role in the ratification of the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments and played a key role in drafting Reconstruction laws allowing Antebellum-Black folks to vote before the ratification of the 14th and 15th Amendments and laws that barred former Confederate States Politians, Military Officers and other wealthy Confederate sympathizers from reclaiming their US Citizenship for 20 years. In 7 Southern States including North Carolina had Super Majority Black voters from 1866 onwards. Therefore, President Abraham Lincoln received all the Electoral College Votes from these states thus enabling him to serve four terms (1861 - 1877).

Post-politics, Davis becomes a trailblazer in the business world, founding several financial institutions, establishing the Atlanta Southern Stock Exchange in Atlanta, Georgia, Oil Tycoon and Billionaire. The film chronicles his journey through the tumultuous Reconstruction era 1865 - 1896, World War I, Prohibition, the Antebellum-Black American Southern Renaissance (1918-1933), and the onset of the Great Depression.

text:
Taraji P. Henson asked for $500,000 to play Brad Pitt's mother. She got $150,000 and says about $30,000 of it was left. The movie made $335 million.

In the video below, Gayle King asks if she's quitting acting. Taraji covers her face and cries before she can say a word. Then she does the math out loud.

In 2008 she was third on the call sheet for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, behind Pitt and Cate Blanchett. Her 2016 memoir says she'd been promised "somewhere in the mid six figures." At a 2023 SAG-AFTRA event she said she asked for $500,000 and was first offered $100,000.

It came up to $150,000 with a condition. She had to cover three months of New Orleans hotel bills herself. "Insult, meet injury," she wrote.

On The Real she did the sum. Half the $150,000 went to taxes. Her team took 30% of the full fee, $45,000. That left $30,000, and her son's school tuition that year was $30,000. "Literally, for five months, that's what I made."

The memoir puts her pay at less than 2% of what the studio paid the top name on that call sheet, Pitt.

She got an Oscar nomination for the role. Fifteen years later she said she almost walked away from The Color Purple over pay. That same month she told Gayle King: "Every time I do something and I break another glass ceiling, when it's time to renegotiate, I'm at the bottom again."

The case for the studio: Pitt sold the tickets, and she doesn't dispute his money. "They deserve to earn what they get," she said of Pitt and Blanchett.

Her side: "I too worked my ass off, and at the time I couldn't say no. I didn't have any power."

$335 million at the box office. An Oscar nomination. One year of school fees.

Every day, one star's real paycheck.

Was that Hollywood paying for box office power, or paying a Black woman less because it could?

GOVARDHAN PUJA: BEFORE WORSHIPPING THE MOUNTAINS, LEARN TO PROTECT NATURE!

Govardhan is not merely a mountain. It is a profound declaration of nature’s victory over human arrogance.

When Lord Krishna lifted Govardhan Hill, He conveyed an extraordinary message to humanity:

Do not search for God somewhere in the heavens. The Divine exists in the flowing rivers, the living trees, the mountains, and in the breath of every creature.

But how strange is the human mind!

Man worships mountains while destroying them.

He offers water to trees while cutting down forests.

He calls the cow his mother, yet abandons her to starve on the streets.

And then, with folded hands, he prays:

“O Lord, please protect us!”

WHAT A MAGNIFICENT HYPOCRISY!

You destroy the very nature that sustains your existence, and then beg God to save you from destruction!

Krishna did not lift Govardhan merely so that future generations could build idols and perform rituals.

His divine act carried a deeper message:

Love nature. Protect the vulnerable. And never surrender before arrogance and injustice.

RELIGION IS NOT WHAT YOU DISPLAY INSIDE A TEMPLE. RELIGION IS WHAT YOU LIVE OUTSIDE IT.

The day you save a tree from destruction, feed a hungry animal, and experience genuine gratitude towards nature—

THAT DAY, YOUR GOVARDHAN PUJA WILL TRULY BE COMPLETE.

Offering flowers to a mountain is easy. Protecting that mountain from destruction is the real test of devotion.

This Govardhan Puja, do not merely light lamps.

LIGHT THE FLAME OF CONSCIOUSNESS WITHIN YOURSELF.

Because the greatest worship of the Creator is to protect His creation.

Wishing everyone a blessed, peaceful and spiritually awakened Govardhan Puja! 🙏🌿

— Narendra Kumar Goswami
Advocate, Supreme Court of India

text:
A giant coil of rope made from human hair (kezuna) on display at Higashi Hongan-ji Temple in Kyoto, Japan 🇯🇵

During the major reconstruction of the temple's massive wooden halls (completed in 1895 after fires), standard hemp ropes were not strong enough to hoist the heavy timber beams into place. In a remarkable act of devotion, female Buddhist followers and donors from across Japan cut off their long hair, which was braided together with hemp into thick, high-strength ropes (kezuna). Fifty-three such ropes were created, with the largest measuring around 110m (360ft) long and weighing close to a ton.

. . .

Higashi Hongan-ji, the "Eastern Temple of the Original Vow," is the head temple of the Ōtani branch of Jōdo Shinshū, one of Japan's largest Buddhist schools. It was founded in Kyoto in 1602 after the original Hongan-ji community split in two. It burned several times during the Edo period, and in 1864 its halls were destroyed again in fires caused by the Kinmon Incident, a failed armed uprising in the imperial capital. Rebuilding began in 1880, and it was a huge undertaking. The new Founder's Hall (Goei-dō) is among the largest wooden buildings in the world, and raising it took enormous timber beams and pillars brought to Kyoto from across the country. Ordinary hemp ropes of the time were too weak for loads like that. They often snapped while hauling the heavy timber, which caused serious accidents.

The temple's female followers offered a solution that has become one of its most remarkable relics. Women from all over Japan cut off their hair and donated it, and it was braided together with hemp into extra-strong ropes called *kezuna* ("hair ropes"). Fifty-three of them were made. The largest was about 110m (360ft) long and 40cm thick, and it weighed close to a tonne. In Meiji-era Japan a woman's long hair was closely tied to her identity and beauty, so these gifts were a deeply personal act of devotion. The ropes helped haul the timber that let the rebuilding finish, and the Founder's Hall and Amida Hall were completed in 1895. One surviving rope, 69m long and weighing about 375 kilograms, is still coiled in a glass case inside the temple grounds as a reminder of the people who literally gave part of themselves to raise it.

text:
CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse : https://t.co/5Gvi3CjR37

"arXiv:2611.09891v1 [https://t.co/gQRNwvACTl] 06 Nov 2026
CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
Peter BelcakGreg HeinrichSaurav MuralidharanShizhe DiaoPavlo MolchanovAbstract
Abstract. Large language models re-invent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.Links: Lab | Project Moonshot: Local Frontier Intelligence
1Introduction
Language models solve every problem from scratch, no matter how common. However, many of their solutions apply not just to the exact problems posed but extend to entire classes of problems in which the individual problem instances vary in their phrasing or some of their parameters. Table 1 illustrates this on an example drawn from a popular mathematical benchmark.OriginalRephrasedReparameterizedQuestionHow many positive whole-number divisors does 196 have?Find how many positive integers evenly divide https://t.co/i254YCqTp1 many positive whole-number divisors does 144 have?ReasoningI need to find the prime factorisation of 196 first. 196=4×49=22×72.
For a number with prime factorisation p1a1×p2a2×⋯, the number of divisors is (a1+1)(a2+1)⋯.
For 196=22×72: (2+1)​(2+1)=3×3=𝟗.I need to find the prime factorisation of 144 first. 144=16×9=24×32.
For a number with prime factorisation p1a1×p2a2×⋯, the number of divisors is (a1+1)(a2+1)⋯.
For 144=24×32: (4+1)​(2+1)=5×3=𝟏𝟓.Table 1:A MATH-500 problem, its rephrasing while keeping all the parameters the same, its reparametrization while keeping the phrasing the same, and the corresponding reasoning traces. The rephrased variant changes only the wording; the reparameterized variant substitutes the numerical parameter and adjusts the arithmetic accordingly. Note how neither the rephrasing nor the reparametrization change even a single word in the reasoning steps leading to the final answer, not to mention their substance.
AI agents and AI-enabled software more broadly often rely on repetitive queries to LLMs featuring the same instructions and plans but different payloads. The LLMs comprehending the same prompts and subsequently reasoning through their tasks from scratch for each new query often results in a significant amount of work being done repeatedly across separate inference instances.System-level caching (SLC) methods aim to address such inefficiencies by recognizing repetitive patterns in LM conversations and caching them at the level of the serving system as a whole rather than within any single inference instance. Maintained at the system level, an SLC’s entries are shared across all of the system’s inference instances and remain reusable beyond the instance in which they were born. SLC methods usually bring one or more of the following benefits:
•Cost and latency reduction. SLC methods can reduce the cost and/or the latency of LLM calls by re-using partial or complete results of earlier LLM calls.
•Improved correctness. SLCs can be reviewed asynchronously by humans or a committee of judge agents to ensure that the responses or steps of the most popular queries are correct.
•Improved explainability or interpretability. SLCs can be inspected by humans to understand the reasoning process and the final answer or result, providing explanation or at the very least an interpretation of responses to popular queries.When choosing or designing an SLC method, the following considerations are important:
•Local robustness. How well does the SLC method cover the class of queries it is supposed to cover? How robust is the SLC method to small perturbations of the queries?
•Correctness upon hit. If the cache is hit, is the result correct? How much confidence can one have in the correctness of the cached result given a hit from the query neighbourhood it covers?
•Explainability or interpretability. How much can one learn by inspecting the caches? How good are the guarantees of correctness provided by the cache entries? Can they be inspected by an authority (e.g., a regulatory body) to provide a guarantee on behavior?
•Cost. How expensive is it to build, maintain, and use the SLC?Existing work on SLC falls into two broad categories:
•Monolithic caching. Methods such as ephemeral prefix caching [1], programmatic conversation caching [2, 3], and semantic query matching [4] look up transcripts of previous conversations on the basis of input prefix overlaps, programmatically supplied conversation IDs, and semantic similarities between different queries. They store entire conversations and their corresponding intermediate generation states (e.g., KV caches or Mamba hidden states) and aim to re-use the largest possible contiguous portion of the query’s generation states wherever possible. Monolithic caches are usually not robust to even the slightest perturbations of the conversation, and when they are (e.g., when employing semantic similarity search), it is often at the expense of their correctness. Monolithic caches of responses can be inspected to guarantee absolute correctness. They are usually compute-cheap to build, maintain, and use but are memory- and bandwidth-expensive to maintain and use.
•Modular caching. Instead of storing the entire conversational transcripts and their generation artifacts, modular SLC methods first perform a mechanical form of decomposition of the existing contexts and their generation states or a distillation of the context into critical logical steps [5, 6, 7]. Later, when encountering an apparently similar problem, the decomposed artifacts are re-supplied to the language model to accelerate their reasoning process. Only parts of the response are cached, and even in the case of a perfect cache hit, a full new generation (though accelerated) of the response is still required. This makes their coverage more robust to parametric perturbations of the inputs but makes it impossible to guarantee correctness upon review. Modular caches sometimes offer interpretable insights into the reasoning process of the underlying models. They are considerably more compute-expensive to build and use than monolithic caches but tend to be more memory- and bandwidth-efficient to maintain and use.We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a (see below) hybrid SLC method that produces agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) that are robust in coverage, can be asynchronously ensured to be correct, are fully explainable, and are cheap to build, maintain, and use. We call them agentic reasoning caches because their elements are small, specialized fractional agents that can be re-used on new parameters. Our approach rests on two observations:
O1Once a particular problem has been reasoned through and the solution has been found, the execution of the solution – the computation or data manipulation behind the problem – can be performed with little involvement from language models. In other words, the search for a solution can be decoupled from the execution of the solution found.
O2Much of LM’s reasoning about a particular problem instance can be reused for a set of problems extending beyond the singleton instance.Leveraging Observation O1, we choose to convert LM conversation transcripts to code, and allow that code to make use of only small language models to perform semantic similarity search and elementary natural language processing tasks such as value extraction, format conversion, classification, or summarization, and only where needed. Leveraging Observation O2, we choose to parametrize the code in a way that allows it to be re-used for all problems that are equirational to the problem solved in the original transcript (i.e., can be solved using the same reasoning). Further, we choose to produce code in such a manner that does not rely on fixed variable, parameter, and function names but on their natural language descriptions and examples, thus allowing for a liberal re-use of all logical components of previously cached logic in all semantically equivalent scenarios, no matter how phrased, structured, or parameterized.Agentic reasoning caching is a hybrid of monolithic and modular SLC because it decomposes the logic of an LLM conversation into a network of modules – semantic functions – that can be re-used individually and also provides their composition into a single function that can be used to solve the problem cached. Because of the semantic functions’ wide parametrization, ARCs are robust to logically valid parametric perturbations of the problem. Since every ARC entry is stored as code, ARCs are fully explainable and correctible upon human or AI inspection. Since ARCs are stored as code using only SLMs, they are cheap to maintain and use since they rely mostly on CPU execution. They are further relatively cheap to build, coming at 12-84x the cost of the original reasoning.Figure 1:Gated use of an agentic reasoning cache. The cache is tried first; on a miss or error, the request falls through to the full LLM.
def serve(request):try:result = cache.use(request)if result is not False:return resultexcept CacheInvocationError:passreturn llm(request)Agentic reasoning caching is particularly suitable for agentic systems that repeatedly use the same prompts with variable payloads. In an agentic system, using an ARC can be attempted before forwarding the request to the cloud LLM, allowing for a significant reduction in the latency and cost in the case of a cache hit. Owing to their reliance on simple CPU execution and SLMs, agentic reasoning caches are so resource-efficient that they can be brought to edge devices, reducing the cost further. Figure 1 briefly illustrates the gated use of an agentic reasoning cache in an AI system where the cache re-use is attempted before forwarding the request to the full LLM.Our contributions are:
C1The introduction of agentic reasoning caching, a hybrid SLC method that is robust in its coverage, can be asynchronously ensured to be correct by human or AI inspection, is fully explainable, and is cheap to build, maintain, and use.
C2The evaluation of agentic reasoning caching on a range of challenging mathematical and science benchmarks, including its success rates, correctness, robustness, and cost-saving capabilities.
C3A brief discussion of the intended placement and implications of this work.Our long-term goal is to bring ARC to real production agents to help lower their cost. In this initial, exploratory work, we deliberately focus on the hardest case: rather than agentic workloads of varied difficulty, we test whether ARCs can match frontier-level model performance on difficult mathematical and scientific benchmarks that are commonly used to measure intelligence. Succeeding at that (as we show we do) indicates that the method is not capped by the ability of models to produce these small ARCs, and that, by extension, the broader class of agentic tasks currently driven by frontier-level models is plausibly cacheable as well.
2Agentic reasoning caching
Let 𝒮,ℬ,𝒯 be the source, builder, and target language model, respectively, and 𝒜 be an answering oracle that answers all queries correctly. Here, the source 𝒮 is the capable, expensive model whose intelligence we aim to cache; the builder ℬ is the model that analyzes 𝒮’s reasoning transcripts and constructs cache entries; and the target 𝒯 is the small, cost-efficient model on which caches are to execute at inference time. Additionally, in some places we make use of LM judges 𝒥, which are simply language models tasked with verifying the correctness and faithfulness of intermediate and final outputs throughout construction and evaluation. Let q(∙1,∙2,…,∙n) be a query template with n parameters.Let q⁡(o) be a query instance submitted for caching with o being a specific value vector for q’s parameters.Assume that 𝒜⁡(q⁡(o)) exists, meaning that q⁡(o) is solvable. Observe that there exists a set of parameter vectors Π such that for all π∈Π, q⁡(π) is equirational to q⁡(o). This is because at the very least, q⁡(o) is equirational to itself.Agentic reasoning caching is based on the following two assumptions:A1For every q⁡(o) that is solvable there exists a program p(∙1,∙2,…,∙n) with access to an SLM such that p⁡(π)=𝒜⁡(q⁡(π)) for all π∈Π.
A2p(∙1,∙2,…,∙n) can be constructed by ℬ from knowing q⁡(o) and 𝒮⁡(q⁡(o)).Assumption A1 effectively amounts to the belief that every solvable problem is solvable with a combination of code and a small language model in a way that extends to all equirational variants of the problem. Assumption A2 expresses the belief that it is possible to encode into p by some language model ℬ the intelligence in 𝒮 required to solve q⁡(o) and its equirational variants using q⁡(o) and its output under 𝒮 as starting points.Agentic reasoning caching is the embodiment of the above assumptions. Implementing Assumption A1, we ask the builder model to analyze source model conversation transcripts to be cached to find which parts (together with their ranges of validity) of their inputs can be varied without requiring substantive changes to the reasoning. Further implementing Assumption A2, we ask the builder model to comprehend the source transcript and construct a program that can solve the problem posed in the original query considering the above-found input parts as parameters that can be varied. To ensure maximal robustness and cache coverage, we insist that the program is a rich composition of independently invokable units representing logical steps that constitute the reasoning process, which we call semantic functions. An agentic reasoning cache is then a set of semantic functions combined with a many-to-one map of problem instances to the natural language descriptions of the semantic functions that can solve the respective instances.The remainder of this section describes the semantic functions that constitute programs p (Section 2.1) and the cache construction (Section 2.2.1) and invocation (Section 2.2.2) processes.
2.1Semantic functions
A semantic function is an executable abstraction representing one logical step of the source reasoning trace, designed to be maximally reusable across semantically equivalent contexts. They are the matter of which agentic reasoning caching is made up. In our implementation, it is simply a Python callable that takes a Context object and returns a dictionary mapping natural-language descriptions to values:f:Context⟶dict[str, Any].Unlike conventional functions whose inputs, outputs, and callees are referenced by fixed identifiers, semantic functions reference everything by natural-language descriptions and examples. This enables semantic discovery: a caller need not know the callee’s name, only a description of what it does, and a callee need not know the names of its inputs, only their descriptions. This design allows any component of a previously cached computation to be reused in any semantically equivalent scenario regardless of how it is phrased or structured (Figure 2). Further, if a change (such as a generalization introducing new parameter) is made to a dependency semantic function, none of its callers need to be updated. Instead, its new, generalized description will open it to a larger set of callers, again without affecting its past callers as long as the new description semantically entails the old one.
Runtime primitives.
Semantic functions are designed to use a small set of runtime primitives that mediate all data flow and computation:
•load(ctx, query): retrieve a value from the layered context memory via vector similarity search. An optional d_type parameter triggers type coercion on the retrieved value.
•do(ctx, query, payloads): discover and invoke another semantic function by natural-language description. Pushes an isolated memory layer pre-populated with the given payloads, executes the matched function, and returns its output dictionary.
•narrate(ctx, message): record a human-readable reasoning step in the narration trace, providing a running explanation of the computation for later inspection.
•lm(ctx, prompt): query the target model 𝒯 for an elementary natural-language processing task such as classification, summarization, or short-form generation.
•extract(ctx, text, prompt): use 𝒯 to perform verbatim value extraction from a piece of text. Supports d_type for type coercion on the extracted value.
•convert(ctx, value, type) / smart_convert(ctx, text, type): multi-tier type coercion. Programmatic conversion is attempted first; if it fails, smart_convert asks 𝒯 to rewrite the value into a Python literal that is then validated by ast.literal_eval().
•invoke_tool(ctx, name, args): call a registered external tool (e.g., terminal or a web search API), enabling semantic functions to integrate with tool-augmented pipelines.
Type safety.
Because values flow between functions through semantic search rather than typed variable bindings, type coercion is critical. Both load and extract accept an optional d_type parameter that coerces the retrieved or extracted value to the desired Python type. When direct coercion fails, smart_convert invokes 𝒯 to rewrite the value into a Python literal, which is then parsed via ast.literal_eval() to ensure syntactic validity and type correctness.
Composition via do and load.
Semantic functions are composed into networks through the do() primitive. The do() primitive invokes a semantic function by describing its intention imperatively in natural language and passing parameters annotated by their natural language descriptions. A caller passes described parameter values into do(), which pushes a fresh, isolated memory layer onto the context stack, populates it with the payloads, and dispatches to the callee found by semantic search over the function registry. The callee accesses its inputs via load() and stores its outputs into the same layer. Upon return, the caller retrieves results from the callee’s output dictionary with load(result, query). This mechanism enables hierarchical decomposition: a root function can delegate to arbitrarily nested sub-functions based on its intention rather than their named identities, with each sub-function operating in its own scope while sharing the underlying context stack. See Figure 5 in Appendix A for a complete cache entry illustrating these primitives on an ideal gas law problem from SciBench.
Context and memory model.
The Context object maintains a stack of memory layers, each backed by a CPU-powered vector store using a small semantic embedding model. When load() is called, it searches the layers top-down, returning the best match from the most local scope. Each invocation of do() pushes a new layer and pops it upon completion, providing natural scoping that prevents unintended interference between sibling calls.

text:
China has secured a “rare window” to narrow the gap with the US in artificial intelligence if the Democrats’ midterm election victory slows American infrastructure expansion, according to analysts.

The technological rivalry between Washington and Beijing has grown fiercer during President Donald Trump’s second term, prompting Chinese policymakers to assess how the Democratic sweep of Congress will reshape global trade and technological competition.

Anticipation of political friction surrounding the multi-trillion-dollar US data center boom has unsettled financial markets and raised concerns over reduced demand for Chinese electronics exports.

Regional markets have fluctuated over expectations that newly elected lawmakers could push for tougher regulatory oversight and tighter permitting on domestic power and computing projects.

Meng Qingyi, a global governance researcher at Tsinghua University, noted that any deceleration in the US offers Beijing an opening to accelerate domestic chip manufacturing, refine algorithm efficiency under constrained compute, and broaden the global adoption of open-source models.

Meng warned that this opening may be short-lived, as bipartisan consensus in Washington remains firmly committed to maintaining an overall American technological advantage.

Gary Ng, senior economist at Natixis, highlighted that while China faces domestic hardware limitations, its advantages in power grid supply, industrial infrastructure, and streamlined data center development could help it leverage any American pause.

Ng added that a weakened US presidency does not automatically guarantee China can leapfrog its rival, noting that major US hyperscalers could simply shift computing investments to overseas jurisdictions.

At the same time, analysts warned that a Democratic-controlled Congress is likely to pursue more rigid curbs on Beijing’s access to American semiconductors, computing equipment, and engineering talent.

Zhang Jun, chief economist at Galaxy Securities, projected that while baseline trade agreements may remain in place, bilateral conflict will center increasingly on advanced computing, supply chain sovereignty, and AI deployment.

Stricter US legislative measures could also target overseas operations set up by Chinese tech giants such as ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent, which frequently utilize international facilities to access cutting-edge chips unavailable at home.

Dan Wang of Eurasia Group observed that the Democrats' institutional approach to tech controls could ultimately pose a more structural obstacle to China's computing ecosystem than the White House's transactional strategy.

Frederic Neumann, chief Asia economist at HSBC, warned that a US infrastructure slowdown would present a clear headwind for Asian exporters supplying American data center projects, even as it potentially cools global component costs and eases supply shortages elsewhere.

Lower component pricing globally could conversely assist Chinese operators in accelerating domestic facility expansions.

A senior researcher at a Shanghai government think-tank remarked that while technological progress remains steady, the initial wave of untamed capital investment is maturing into a more ruthless phase of resource allocation.

Beijing’s official reaction to the election outcome has remained restrained, with foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun calling the midterms an internal US matter and affirming China's desire for a stable bilateral relationship.

text:
Chinese AI lab Moonshot has sought access to advanced Nvidia chips hosted at data centers in Europe, sources told CNBC, as U.S. export controls continue to restrict direct shipments to China.

Deals have been discussed this year for Beijing-based Moonshot to rent capacity from European "neoclouds" hosting Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs).

U.S. export controls serve as a central tool in Washington's strategy to maintain a lead over China in the artificial intelligence race, where American labs like OpenAI and Anthropic face mounting competition from Chinese rivals.

Moonshot specifically aimed to lease capacity powered by Nvidia's advanced Blackwell systems, which are barred from direct import into China.

Remote access through overseas facilities offers an operational loophole, as current U.S. regulations do not grant broad oversight over foreign cloud computing arrangements.

The European discussions follow claims by the White House in July that Moonshot had previously accessed Nvidia Blackwell chips through a data center in Thailand.

Neither Moonshot, Nvidia, the White House, nor Chinese officials responded to requests for comment.

Sources familiar with the discussions described Moonshot as "very aggressive" in pursuing European compute, holding talks to secure clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs for inference as well as model training.

Racing to secure computing power

Founded in 2023, Moonshot has emerged as one of China’s prominent model developers, seeing surging demand following the July launch of its Kimi K3 model.

Heavy user uptake previously stretched Moonshot's infrastructure, prompting the lab to temporarily pause new subscriptions while securing additional compute capacity.

In the compute-leasing market, providers and financiers have weighed higher pricing for Chinese clients, with one source noting a proposal requiring Moonshot to pay 30% to 50% more upfront than non-Chinese customers to hedge against regulatory risks.

Political pressure

Washington lawmakers have sought to close the cloud loophole through the proposed Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which cleared the House in January but remains pending in the Senate.

Concurrently, reports indicate Nvidia instructed cloud partners to ensure at least 51% of their services go to non-Chinese customers.

In response to the developments, an Nvidia spokesperson argued that American AI infrastructure must lead globally to prevent foreign-built hardware and software from dominating cloud ecosystems.

Separately, Nvidia noted that while U.S. officials licensed shipments of older H200 chips earlier this year, Chinese authorities restricted those purchases to support domestic chipmakers.

text:
Jensen Huang’s affair: the cheapest weapon in this storm.
The New York Times revealed in late October that Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, had been identified by U.S. intelligence as an asset recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security. Her mission: get close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, gather intelligence on advanced chips, and possibly help reroute controlled chips to China through third countries. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had already circulated a classified memo to senior White House officials before the May summit. That is the core of this story.
But the moment public attention actually shifted was November 8th, when Huang himself sent a letter to employees admitting he had been unfaithful to his wife. By confessing in his own words, he converted the hardest question to answer — whether chips flowed to China — into the easiest one to dismiss: a personal failing. You want to investigate chip exports? He only has to say: I was wrong. I’m sorry.
This is not a coincidence. Sexual scandal requires no evidence. Spying demands investigation, proof, time. An affair needs only one sentence. And once the frame becomes “a man who cheated,” every question about export controls, about Megaspeed’s 136,000 GPUs, about why the Commerce Department kept licensing NewMatrix — a company with an empty office and no traceable business — gets buried under moral outrage.
Both parties are playing the same game from opposite sides. Republicans use national security as the pretext; Democrats use anti-corruption. Trump calls Huang “an honorable guy” and offers to take him on the Asia trip. Warren and Coons demand testimony and subpoenas. Bernstein’s analysts warned the worst-case beneficiary is China itself — because if Huang is forced out, the one executive who understood both Washington and Beijing is gone, and the regulatory vacuum favors Beijing.
The affair is real. The damage to his family is real. But treating it as the story, rather than the distraction, is the oldest trick in politics: when you cannot win the argument, change the subject to something no one can defend.

📞 Finland and Norway called Putin partly to assess his state of mind — Politico.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a roughly 90-minute conversation with Putin on October 27, ahead of renewed Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

Støre described Putin’s conduct as “rational” and “professional.” But the conversation did not convince him that Russia’s leader was genuinely ready for a peace deal.

▪️ The Nordic leaders consulted Zelenskyy beforehand and briefed him afterwards.
▪️ They conveyed Ukraine’s position: de-escalation first, with territorial questions addressed directly between heads of state.
▪️ Baltic Sea security and keeping maritime trade routes open were also discussed.

Støre denied reports that Putin had used the call to deliver a lecture on Slavic history.

The initiative divided European allies. Its supporters argued that Washington should not be the only Western voice reaching the Kremlin. Critics warned that renewed engagement could reward Russian aggression.

Putin’s willingness to answer the phone offered an opening for diplomacy. His willingness to end the war remained unproven.

China has signed a free trade agreement with Peru, and one port in particular stands out: the Port of Chancay. However, some Western media outlets exaggerate the significance of the port to portray China in a negative light.

What does Chancay actually look like, and what is it really capable of? We visited the port to find out.
· Chancay is a smart port, with automated trucks, cranes and a digital control center. Chinese electric vehicles arrive, while Peruvian fruit, minerals and other regional exports move in the opposite direction.
· The direct Chancay–Shanghai service takes about 23 days, roughly 10 days faster than routes involving intermediate stops.
· For a country whose economy depends heavily on international trade, Chancay offers something important. A chance to move from being only an exporter of raw materials toward becoming a regional logistics and commercial hub.

Chancay is growing fast, but remains small by global standards. Yet some Western narratives portray it as a threat simply because it was built by a Chinese company.

And it's also about mindset. Too much Western coverage still treats Latin America as someone else's backyard, a region free to choose its partners only when Washington approves. But if useful projects are blocked, it will not be politicians or headline writers who pay the price. It will be local workers, exporters and families. #MediaUnlocked
